axiam_sdk

Official Python client SDK for AXIAM (Access eXtended Identity and Authorization Management).

Re-exports the public surface: the sync AxiamClient and async AsyncAxiamClient REST entry points, the AuthError/AuthzError/ NetworkError exception taxonomy (CONTRACT.md §2), and the request/response models (LoginResult, User, AccessCheck, AccessResult, BatchCheckResult, UserInfo). See CONTRACT.md §1-§10 for the cross-language behavioral contract this SDK conforms to.

Also re-exports CONTRACT.md §28's two framework-agnostic MCP resource-server operations, protected_resource_metadata and bearer_challenge (RFC 9728

  • RFC 6750) — both pure, I/O-free computation, like uma_parse_challenge. The third, serve_protected_resource_metadata, registers a route and is therefore framework-specific; find it on axiam_sdk.fastapi and axiam_sdk.django.

This module MUST remain importable with ONLY the runtime dependencies declared in [project.dependencies] (httpx, grpcio, aio-pika, pydantic, PyJWT) — the optional web-framework integrations (axiam_sdk.fastapi, axiam_sdk.django, see [project.optional-dependencies]) MUST NOT be imported from here.

  9cross-language behavioral contract this SDK conforms to.

class RevocationFeed: 
100class RevocationFeed:
101    """A poller for one deployment's revocation feed.
102
103    Share one instance across the guards that should poll once between them,
104    rather than once each. Thread-safe.
105    """
106
107    def __init__(
108        self,
109        base_url: str,
110        *,
111        poll_interval_seconds: float = DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
112        client: httpx.Client | None = None,
113        now: Any = time.monotonic,
114    ) -> None:
115        """Build a poller against ``{base_url}/oauth2/revocations``.
116
117        Args:
118            base_url: The AXIAM server's base URL;
119                :data:`REVOCATION_FEED_PATH` is appended after stripping any
120                trailing slash.
121            poll_interval_seconds: How often a guard's first call after this
122                many seconds refetches the document. Raised to
123                :data:`MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` if lower — the server caches
124                the feed for that long, so polling faster costs requests and
125                buys no freshness.
126            client: An ``httpx.Client`` to fetch through, for callers that
127                pin a transport, a proxy or a CA bundle. A per-call client
128                with a bounded timeout is used when omitted.
129            now: The monotonic clock, injected so tests can pin staleness
130                without sleeping.
131        """
132        self._feed_url = base_url.rstrip("/") + REVOCATION_FEED_PATH
133        self._poll_interval = max(poll_interval_seconds, MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
134        self._client = client
135        self._now = now
136        # ``None`` means "never successfully fetched", which is NOT the same as
137        # an empty set — and is why this is not a bare ``set``.
138        self._entries: set[str] | None = None
139        self._last_attempt: float | None = None
140        self._lock = threading.Lock()
141
142    def is_revoked(self, sid: str) -> bool:
143        """Has this session been revoked, as far as this poller knows?
144
145        ``False`` whenever the answer is not a confident yes — a feed never
146        fetched, unreachable, malformed, or simply not listing this session.
147        The caller admits the request in all of those cases, which is §10.4
148        rule 3 and is the whole reason the feature is safe to turn on.
149        """
150        self._refresh_if_stale()
151        with self._lock:
152            entries = self._entries
153        return entries is not None and revocation_entry_for(sid) in entries
154
155    def refresh(self) -> None:
156        """Fetch now, whatever the interval says. For tests, and for warming."""
157        fetched = self._fetch_once()
158        with self._lock:
159            self._last_attempt = self._now()
160            if fetched is not None:
161                self._entries = fetched
162            # On failure the previous set is deliberately left in place: a blip
163            # must not un-revoke a session the guard already knows about.
164
165    def _refresh_if_stale(self) -> None:
166        """Refetch if the poll interval has elapsed since the last *attempt*.
167
168        Attempt, not success: a feed that is down must not be retried on every
169        request, which would put the request path back on the network — the
170        cost §10.4 exists to avoid.
171        """
172        with self._lock:
173            last = self._last_attempt
174            due = last is None or (self._now() - last) >= self._poll_interval
175        if due:
176            self.refresh()
177
178    def _fetch_once(self) -> set[str] | None:
179        """One fetch. ``None`` for every kind of failure, which the caller
180        treats identically — see the module docstring on why "unusable" must
181        not collapse into "empty"."""
182        try:
183            if self._client is not None:
184                response = self._client.get(self._feed_url)
185            else:
186                response = httpx.get(self._feed_url, timeout=5.0)
187            if response.status_code != 200:
188                return None
189            document = response.json()
190        except Exception:
191            return None
192        if not isinstance(document, dict):
193            return None
194        if document.get("alg") != _SUPPORTED_ALG:
195            return None
196        revoked = document.get("revoked")
197        if not isinstance(revoked, list) or len(revoked) > MAX_ENTRIES:
198            return None
199        return {entry for entry in revoked if isinstance(entry, str)}

Args: base_url: The AXIAM server's base URL; REVOCATION_FEED_PATH is appended after stripping any trailing slash. poll_interval_seconds: How often a guard's first call after this many seconds refetches the document. Raised to MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS if lower — the server caches the feed for that long, so polling faster costs requests and buys no freshness. client: An httpx.Client to fetch through, for callers that pin a transport, a proxy or a CA bundle. A per-call client with a bounded timeout is used when omitted. now: The monotonic clock, injected so tests can pin staleness without sleeping.

142    def is_revoked(self, sid: str) -> bool:
143        """Has this session been revoked, as far as this poller knows?
144
145        ``False`` whenever the answer is not a confident yes — a feed never
146        fetched, unreachable, malformed, or simply not listing this session.
147        The caller admits the request in all of those cases, which is §10.4
148        rule 3 and is the whole reason the feature is safe to turn on.
149        """
150        self._refresh_if_stale()
151        with self._lock:
152            entries = self._entries
153        return entries is not None and revocation_entry_for(sid) in entries

89def revocation_entry_for(sid: str) -> str:
90    """The feed entry for a ``sid``, as the server computes it.
91
92    Base64url without padding over the claim's **exact string** — never a
93    parsed and re-rendered UUID, or the answer depends on this SDK's parser
94    rather than on the feed.
95    """
96    digest = hashlib.sha256(sid.encode("utf-8")).digest()
97    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(digest).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")

class DecisionMemo: 
 92class DecisionMemo:
 93    """A bounded, TTL-clamped decision memo.
 94
 95    ``ttl_ms == 0`` means **disabled** — not "cache for zero milliseconds".
 96    That is the default, and both :meth:`get` and :meth:`set` become no-ops.
 97
 98    Thread-safe: the sync client is commonly shared across a thread pool, and a
 99    cache that corrupted under concurrency would be a worse bug than the one it
100    is optimising away.
101    """
102
103    __slots__ = ("_ttl_ms", "_entries", "_now", "_lock")
104
105    def __init__(self, ttl_ms: float = 0.0, now: Callable[[], float] | None = None) -> None:
106        """
107        :param ttl_ms: requested TTL in milliseconds; ``0`` disables the memo and
108            any value above :data:`MAX_TTL_MS` is clamped to it.
109        :param now: injected monotonic clock in seconds, so the TTL can be
110            tested without waiting.
111        """
112        self._ttl_ms = min(max(float(ttl_ms), 0.0), MAX_TTL_MS)
113        self._entries: OrderedDict[str, tuple[object, float]] = OrderedDict()
114        self._now = now if now is not None else time.monotonic
115        self._lock = threading.Lock()
116
117    @property
118    def enabled(self) -> bool:
119        """Whether this memo does anything. ``False`` for the default config."""
120        return self._ttl_ms > 0
121
122    @property
123    def effective_ttl_ms(self) -> float:
124        """The TTL after clamping."""
125        return self._ttl_ms
126
127    def get(self, key: str) -> object | None:
128        """A live decision for *key*, if one is memoized and unexpired."""
129        if not self.enabled:
130            return None
131        with self._lock:
132            entry = self._entries.get(key)
133            if entry is None:
134                return None
135            decision, stored_at = entry
136            if (self._now() - stored_at) * 1000.0 >= self._ttl_ms:
137                del self._entries[key]
138                return None
139            # Returned whole, including ``reason_code``: §17.1 rule 5 forbids
140            # returning ``allowed`` while dropping the code, which would make
141            # the field intermittently absent — worse than never having had it.
142            return decision
143
144    def set(self, key: str, decision: object) -> None:
145        """Memoize a decision the server actually returned.
146
147        Callers must only reach here on success. §17.1 rule 7 forbids
148        negative-caching a failure: memoizing a transport error as a deny would
149        turn a blip into a TTL-long outage, and memoizing it as an allow is
150        unthinkable.
151        """
152        if not self.enabled:
153            return
154        with self._lock:
155            self._entries.pop(key, None)
156            self._entries[key] = (decision, self._now())
157            while len(self._entries) > _MAX_ENTRIES:
158                self._entries.popitem(last=False)
159
160    def clear(self) -> None:
161        """Drop every entry (§17.1 rule 9).
162
163        Called on login, verify_mfa, refresh and logout. Entries are keyed by
164        subject, not by session, so a re-authentication as a *different*
165        principal would otherwise read the previous principal's decisions.
166        """
167        with self._lock:
168            self._entries.clear()
169
170    def report_clamp(self, requested_ms: float, telemetry: TelemetryDispatcher) -> None:
171        """Emit a :class:`ConfigClamped` if the requested TTL was clamped (§19.2 rule 6).
172
173        This is the clamp that matters most to get right: an operator who set a
174        60-second TTL believes their staleness bound is 60 seconds. It is five,
175        and without this event nothing anywhere says so.
176
177        Nothing is emitted when the requested value was already inside the
178        limit, or when the memo is disabled — an event that fires when nothing
179        happened trains its reader to ignore it.
180        """
181        if not telemetry.installed or requested_ms <= 0.0 or requested_ms == self._ttl_ms:
182            return
183        telemetry.emit(
184            ConfigClamped(
185                setting="decision_memo_ttl_ms",
186                requested=str(requested_ms),
187                effective=str(self._ttl_ms),
188                contract_reference="§17.1 rule 2",
189            )
190        )
191
192    def __len__(self) -> int:
193        """Number of live entries, for tests."""
194        with self._lock:
195            return len(self._entries)

class AxiamClient(axiam_sdk._client._AxiamClientBase, axiam_sdk.management.ops.ManagementNamespaces): 
1104class AxiamClient(_AxiamClientBase, ManagementNamespaces):
1105    """The AXIAM SDK's sync REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10).
1106
1107    ``client.login(...)`` returns a typed :class:`~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult`
1108    with ``mfa_required`` (SC#1). For the async twin, use
1109    :class:`~axiam_sdk.AsyncAxiamClient` (SDK-Q08) — a separate class, not an
1110    ``async_*`` method on this one.
1111    """
1112
1113    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1114    # Lifecycle (D-19)
1115    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1116
1117    def __enter__(self) -> AxiamClient:
1118        """Context-manager entry — returns ``self`` (D-19); no separate
1119        setup beyond what ``__init__`` already did."""
1120        return self
1121
1122    def __exit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
1123        """Context-manager exit — always calls :meth:`close`, regardless of
1124        whether the ``with`` block raised (D-19)."""
1125        self.close()
1126
1127    def close(self) -> None:
1128        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
1129
1130        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
1131        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
1132
1133        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
1134        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
1135        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
1136        restart and resume; a ``close()`` that logged out would silently end
1137        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
1138        ending the session is what you want.
1139
1140        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
1141        rather than silently reconnecting.
1142        """
1143        self._closed = True
1144        self._decision_memo.clear()
1145        self._session.close()
1146
1147    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1148    # acting tenant (CONTRACT.md §5.2 rule 1, contract 1.51)
1149    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1150
1151    def acting_tenant(self, tenant_id: str) -> AxiamClient:
1152        """A handle to this client that acts on ``tenant_id`` — CONTRACT.md
1153        §5.2 rule 1 (contract 1.51).
1154
1155        The returned handle shares everything with ``self`` — session,
1156        cookie jar, refresh guard, telemetry, decision memo — and differs
1157        only in the ``X-Axiam-Tenant`` it sends. ``self`` is unchanged, so
1158        two tasks can act on two tenants at once over one session. Call
1159        :meth:`clear_acting_tenant` on the returned handle (or on ``self``)
1160        to act on the principal's own tenant again.
1161
1162        Meaningful only for an **organization-level** principal; see the
1163        ``acting_tenant`` constructor parameter for what the header does and
1164        does not reach (not ``X-Tenant-ID``, not a ``{tenant_id}`` path, not
1165        gRPC).
1166
1167        Raises:
1168            NetworkError: if ``tenant_id`` is not a UUID.
1169            AuthzError: when this client holds a login result that reported
1170                the principal's reach: if it reported
1171                ``organization_level: False`` (an ordinary tenant principal
1172                is a principal of one tenant, and the server answers ``403``
1173                to anything else), or if it reported ``reachable_tenant_ids``
1174                that does not contain ``tenant_id`` (§5.2.3 rule 4). A client
1175                holding no such result — a service account from client
1176                credentials or the device login, an injected token, a
1177                session completed without a user object — has nothing to
1178                gate on, so the handle is returned and the server's ``403``
1179                is the answer. An organization-level **service account** is
1180                a supported design, and the server honours the header for
1181                one on the terms it does for a user.
1182
1183        There is no string-vs-UUID ambiguity to resolve: the server silently
1184        ignores a value that is not a UUID and answers for the caller's own
1185        tenant instead, so refusing a non-UUID client-side is the refusal.
1186        """
1187        normalized = self._check_acting_tenant_gate(tenant_id)
1188        handle = copy.copy(self)
1189        handle._acting_tenant = normalized
1190        return handle
1191
1192    def clear_acting_tenant(self) -> AxiamClient:
1193        """A handle to this client that sends **no** ``X-Axiam-Tenant`` — the
1194        clear form CONTRACT.md §5.2 rule 1 requires. The principal then acts
1195        on its own tenant. Everything else is shared with ``self``, as for
1196        :meth:`acting_tenant`."""
1197        handle = copy.copy(self)
1198        handle._acting_tenant = None
1199        return handle
1200
1201    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1202    # mTLS device login (CONTRACT.md §6.1 rules 6-10, contract 1.51)
1203    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1204
1205    def authenticate_device(self) -> DeviceToken:
1206        """``POST /api/v1/auth/device`` (CONTRACT.md §6.1) — the mTLS device
1207        login. No request body; returns a typed :class:`DeviceToken` and
1208        adopts ``access_token`` as this client's credential, exactly as a
1209        successful :meth:`login` is adopted.
1210
1211        **Reachable only on a client configured with a client certificate**
1212        (``client_cert``/``client_key`` — see the constructor). Without one
1213        the server would answer ``401`` regardless, so this refuses
1214        client-side instead, with zero wire calls (rule 7).
1215
1216        There is **no refresh token** (D-6 of the dogfooding remediation
1217        plan): a later ``401`` on this credential is surfaced as
1218        :class:`~axiam_sdk.AuthError` without a refresh attempt — call this
1219        method again, which costs one TLS handshake.
1220
1221        Raises:
1222            AuthError: with zero wire calls, if this client was not built
1223                with a client certificate (rule 7); or, from the server,
1224                for an unknown, untrusted, expired, revoked or unbound
1225                certificate, or a ``Server``-type certificate (rule 8 — every
1226                refusal is a ``401``, surfaced with the server's own message).
1227            NetworkError: for a ``429`` (rate-limited; not an authentication
1228                failure, rule 8) or any other transport/status failure.
1229        """
1230        self._ensure_open()
1231        self._reachable_only_with_client_cert("authenticate_device")
1232        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", DEVICE_AUTH_PATH)
1233        # This call is itself a login: withhold the jar explicitly, rather
1234        # than relying on _apply_bearer_credential, which only overrides
1235        # Cookie once a bearer token is already held — never true on the
1236        # very call that is about to mint one. Without this, a cookie left
1237        # by an earlier login() on this client rides along on the request
1238        # that is supposed to authenticate as the device alone, and the
1239        # server reads axiam_access before Authorization (CONTRACT.md §6.1).
1240        request.headers["Cookie"] = ""
1241        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1242        return self._handle_device_auth_response(response)
1243
1244    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1245    # login / verify_mfa
1246    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1247
1248    def login(self, email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
1249        """``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` (CONTRACT.md §1). Returns a typed
1250        :class:`LoginResult`; check ``mfa_required`` before assuming the
1251        session is established (SC#1)."""
1252        self._ensure_open()
1253        self._on_credential_change()
1254        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1255            "POST", LOGIN_PATH, json=self._login_body(email, password)
1256        )
1257        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1258        return self._handle_login_response(response)
1259
1260    def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
1261        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
1262
1263        Returns the same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
1264        ``mfa_required`` case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.
1265
1266        What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither
1267        useful without the account's registration record **and** the tenant's
1268        OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request
1269        log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password,
1270        because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database
1271        is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not
1272        offer. It does **not** protect against a compromised AXIAM server.
1273
1274        Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server
1275        proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the
1276        server during the handshake, so opening ``KE2`` *is* the proof that it
1277        holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an ``M2`` check in
1278        capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now
1279        nothing to skip.
1280
1281        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
1282            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
1283            SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not ``AuthError``: reporting a
1284            configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to
1285            reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to
1286            :meth:`login`.
1287        :raises AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist,
1288            an account with no registration record, and a server that does not
1289            hold the record — indistinguishable by design. **Nothing is sent to
1290            ``login/finish`` in that case** (§23.4 rule 7).
1291
1292        **The ``mode`` field decides what happens after a failed exchange**, and
1293        nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). ``login/start`` carries the tenant's
1294        ``opaque_mode``:
1295
1296        * ``"optional"`` — this method retries over :meth:`login` with the same
1297          credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's
1298          outcome. Under ``optional`` an account with no record is the ordinary
1299          case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an
1300          operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a
1301          password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every
1302          user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state ``optional`` exists
1303          to serve.
1304        * ``"required"``, an unrecognised value, or **no ``mode`` at all** (a
1305          server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is
1306          retried over :meth:`login`. It would be refused anyway: ``required``
1307          answers ``403 opaque_required`` for every principal in the tenant, so
1308          trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.
1309
1310        ``mode`` is **not** downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a
1311        hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer ``404`` and get
1312        the fallback whatever it puts here. ``required`` is what closes that,
1313        server-side, by refusing ``/auth/login`` before examining any
1314        credential.
1315
1316        This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by
1317        default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is
1318        the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by
1319        someone holding the OPRF seed.
1320        """
1321        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
1322
1323        self._ensure_open()
1324        self._on_credential_change()
1325
1326        exchange = start_login(password)
1327
1328        # One round trip, always. SRP had to guess a group before the server
1329        # named one and restart the exchange if it guessed wrong; ``KE1`` does
1330        # not depend on the KSF.
1331        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1332            "POST",
1333            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
1334            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
1335        )
1336        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1337        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
1338            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
1339        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
1340
1341        try:
1342            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
1343        except AuthError:
1344            # §23.4 rule 7. `KE3` is not sent either way; `mode` — and only
1345            # `mode` — decides whether the plaintext path may be tried.
1346            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
1347                raise
1348            return self.login(username_or_email, password)
1349
1350        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1351            "POST",
1352            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
1353            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
1354        )
1355        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1356        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
1357            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
1358        return self._handle_login_response(response)
1359
1360    def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1361        """Build a registration record sealed against the tenant this client is
1362        **acting on**.
1363
1364        That is the right tenant when the record is for an account being created
1365        in it — §27 ``users.create``, and the reset-completion flow, which names
1366        its own tenant. It is the **wrong** tenant for the caller's own password
1367        change once an organization-level principal has selected another one to
1368        act on: the account's credentials live where the account does. Use
1369        :meth:`opaque_enrollment_for_self` there — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2.
1370
1371        The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to
1372        arrive with the request or not at all.
1373
1374        Performs a ``register/start`` round trip, which the SRP verifier this
1375        replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's
1376        oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid
1377        record.
1378
1379        Note the absence of an ``identity`` argument. The SRP version required
1380        the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a
1381        verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential
1382        identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.
1383
1384        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
1385            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
1386            SDK cannot perform.
1387        """
1388        return self._enroll(password, None)
1389
1390    def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1391        """Build a registration record for the **caller's own** new password,
1392        sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.
1393
1394        CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2. ``POST /auth/password/change`` and the record
1395        that accompanies it are about the account, not about whatever tenant the
1396        client is currently pointed at, and a record sealed against the acting
1397        tenant is refused with *"the OPAQUE session was issued for a different
1398        tenant"*.
1399
1400        The distinction only bites for an organization-level principal that has
1401        selected another tenant to act on; for everyone else the two tenants are
1402        the same value and this behaves identically to
1403        :meth:`opaque_enrollment`. It is still the method to call for a
1404        self-service password change, because which principal is signed in is
1405        not something the call site usually knows.
1406
1407        :raises NetworkError: when no login has completed on this client yet —
1408            the principal tenant is reported by the login response, so there is
1409            nothing to seal against before then — and on the same terms as
1410            :meth:`opaque_enrollment` otherwise.
1411        """
1412        if self._principal_tenant_id is None:
1413            raise NetworkError(
1414                "OPAQUE: no principal tenant is known yet — sign in before "
1415                "building a registration record for your own password"
1416            )
1417        return self._enroll(password, self._principal_tenant_id)
1418
1419    def _enroll(self, password: str, principal_tenant_id: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
1420        """The shared body of the two enrolment methods; they differ only in the
1421        tenant the record is sealed against."""
1422        from ._opaque import KsfParams, start_registration
1423
1424        self._ensure_open()
1425        exchange = start_registration(password)
1426
1427        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1428            "POST",
1429            OPAQUE_REGISTER_START_PATH,
1430            json=self._opaque_register_start_body(exchange.request, principal_tenant_id),
1431        )
1432        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1433        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
1434            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "register/start")
1435        started = response.json()
1436
1437        return {
1438            "opaque_session": started["opaque_session"],
1439            "registration_record": exchange.finish(
1440                password, started["registration_response"], KsfParams.from_wire(started)
1441            ),
1442        }
1443
1444    def verify_mfa(self, mfa_token: Any, code: str) -> LoginResult:
1445        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — completes the
1446        two-phase flow started by :meth:`login` when ``mfa_required`` was
1447        true."""
1448        self._ensure_open()
1449        self._on_credential_change()
1450        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1451            "POST", MFA_VERIFY_PATH, json=self._mfa_verify_body(mfa_token, code)
1452        )
1453        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1454        return self._handle_login_response(response)
1455
1456    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1457    # refresh
1458    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1459
1460    def refresh(self) -> None:
1461        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
1462        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
1463        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
1464        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
1465        self._ensure_open()
1466        self._on_credential_change()
1467        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
1468        if not observed_access:
1469            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
1470
1471        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
1472        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
1473        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
1474        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
1475        self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_sync(
1476            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_sync(tenant_id, org_id)
1477        )
1478
1479    def _do_refresh_sync(self, tenant_id: str, org_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1480        """Perform the actual ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` call — the
1481        ``do_refresh`` closure passed to
1482        :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.refresh_if_needed_sync`
1483        by :meth:`refresh`. Not called directly by SDK users; always routed
1484        through the single-flight guard so concurrent 401s collapse into
1485        one in-flight call (§9)."""
1486        # The literal /api/v1/auth/refresh path is required so the
1487        # Path-scoped axiam_refresh cookie attaches (Pitfall 4).
1488        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1489            "POST", "/api/v1/auth/refresh", json=self._refresh_body(tenant_id, org_id)
1490        )
1491        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1492        return self._handle_refresh_response(response)
1493
1494    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1495    # logout
1496    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1497
1498    def logout(self) -> None:
1499        """``POST /api/v1/auth/logout`` (CONTRACT.md §1)."""
1500        self._ensure_open()
1501        self._on_credential_change()
1502        session_id = self._session_id_for_logout()
1503        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1504            "POST", LOGOUT_PATH, json={"session_id": session_id}
1505        )
1506        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1507        if response.status_code >= 300:
1508            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "logout failed", response=response)
1509        self._session.refresh_guard = type(self._session.refresh_guard)()
1510        # CONTRACT.md §6.1 rule 4 / CONTRACT 1.52 N4.4: logout clears a
1511        # held device credential, same as it clears the cookie session.
1512        self._session.clear_bearer_credential()
1513        # §5.2 rule 1: no session, no reach to gate `acting_tenant()` on.
1514        self._principal_scope = None
1515
1516    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1517    # REST authz: check_access / can / batch_check (Task 3)
1518    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1519
1520    def check_access(
1521        self,
1522        action: str,
1523        resource_id: str,
1524        scope: str | None = None,
1525        *,
1526        subject_id: str | None = None,
1527    ) -> AccessResult:
1528        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
1529
1530        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
1531        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
1532        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
1533        declarative ``require_access`` helpers (§11) pass to check the
1534        *request's* authenticated user.
1535        """
1536        self._ensure_open()
1537        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
1538        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
1539        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id, self._acting_tenant)
1540        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
1541        if memoized is not None:
1542            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
1543            return memoized
1544
1545        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
1546        wire = self._authz_post_sync(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
1547        result = AccessResult(**wire)
1548
1549        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
1550        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
1551        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
1552        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
1553        return result
1554
1555    def can(self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None) -> bool:
1556        """Alias for ``check_access`` returning only the allowed boolean
1557        (CONTRACT.md §1 note, browser/UI scenarios)."""
1558        return self.check_access(action, resource_id, scope).allowed
1559
1560    def batch_check(self, checks: list[AccessCheck]) -> list[AccessResult]:
1561        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check/batch`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — results
1562        returned in the same order as ``checks``."""
1563        self._ensure_open()
1564        body = {"checks": [c.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for c in checks]}
1565        wire = self._authz_post_sync(BATCH_CHECK_PATH, body, operation="batch_check")
1566        return BatchCheckResult(**wire).results
1567
1568    def _authz_post_sync(
1569        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], *, operation: str
1570    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1571        """POST an authz request body to *path* under the §16 retry policy.
1572
1573        The call is a ``POST`` but changes no server state, so it is
1574        retry-eligible: §16.2's test is "changes no server state", NOT "is a
1575        GET". Gating on the verb would exclude the single most important
1576        operation this policy covers.
1577
1578        The §9.3 refresh-then-retry-once on a 401 is a *different* mechanism and
1579        stays inside one §16 attempt: a 401 means the token expired, which
1580        refreshing fixes, and neither backing off nor counting it against the
1581        transport-failure budget would make sense.
1582        """
1583        return retry_sync(
1584            lambda attempt: self._authz_post_sync_once(path, body, operation, attempt),
1585            operation=operation,
1586            enabled=self._retry_enabled,
1587            telemetry=self._telemetry,
1588        )
1589
1590    def _authz_post_sync_once(
1591        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], operation: str, attempt: int
1592    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1593        """One §16 attempt, with its §19 request pair."""
1594        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
1595        with self._telemetry.request(operation, "POST", path, attempt) as span:
1596            response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1597
1598            # CONTRACT.md §6.1 rule 5 / CONTRACT 1.52 N4.5: a device
1599            # credential is never refreshed, on either transport. Leaving
1600            # `response` as the server's own 401 when one is held means the
1601            # status check below raises with the SERVER's message, never
1602            # the refresh guard's "no access token to refresh".
1603            if (
1604                response.status_code == httpx.codes.UNAUTHORIZED
1605                and self._session.bearer_token is None
1606            ):
1607                response = self._retry_after_refresh_sync(request)
1608
1609            span.status = response.status_code
1610            if response.status_code < 200 or response.status_code >= 300:
1611                raise error_from_http_status(
1612                    response.status_code, "authz check failed", response=response
1613                )
1614            span.outcome = "success"
1615            result: dict[str, Any] = response.json()
1616            return result
1617
1618    def _retry_after_refresh_sync(self, original_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
1619        """On a 401, refresh exactly once (via the shared single-flight
1620        guard) then retry the failed authz call exactly once. A second
1621        failure propagates through the caller's own status check (§9.3, no
1622        retry loop)."""
1623        self.refresh()
1624        retry_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1625            original_request.method,
1626            original_request.url,
1627            content=original_request.content,
1628            headers={
1629                k: v
1630                for k, v in original_request.headers.items()
1631                if k.lower() not in ("content-length", "x-csrf-token")
1632            },
1633        )
1634        return self._rest_send_sync(retry_request)
1635
1636    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1637    # OIDC / SSO relying-party helpers (CONTRACT.md §12, Task T3)
1638    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1639
1640    def oidc_discover(self) -> OidcConfiguration:
1641        """``GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1642        fetch the OIDC discovery document, cached per origin with a
1643        ≥5-minute TTL and single-flight de-duplication of concurrent calls
1644        (§12.3 rule 6)."""
1645
1646        def fetch() -> OidcConfiguration:
1647            """Perform the actual discovery-document GET; called by the
1648            discovery cache at most once per cache miss/expiry."""
1649            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("GET", DISCOVERY_PATH)
1650            response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1651            return self._parse_discovery_response(response)
1652
1653        return self._discovery_cache.get_sync(self._discovery_origin_key(), fetch)
1654
1655    def oidc_begin(
1656        self,
1657        *,
1658        configuration: OidcConfiguration,
1659        redirect_uri: str,
1660        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1661        extra_params: dict[str, str] | None = None,
1662    ) -> AuthorizationRequest:
1663        """Build an authorization request (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — **pure
1664        local computation, no network I/O**. Nothing is stored: persist
1665        the returned ``state``, ``nonce``, and ``code_verifier`` yourself
1666        (§12.3 rule 1)."""
1667        return self._oidc_begin_impl(
1668            configuration=configuration,
1669            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1670            scope=scope,
1671            extra_params=extra_params,
1672        )
1673
1674    def oidc_par(
1675        self,
1676        *,
1677        request: AuthorizationRequest,
1678        redirect_uri: str,
1679        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1680        dpop_jkt: str | None = None,
1681        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1682        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1683    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
1684        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
1685        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
1686        with.
1687
1688        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
1689        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
1690        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
1691        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
1692        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
1693        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
1694
1695        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
1696        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
1697        authorize any other way (§21.1).
1698
1699        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
1700        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
1701
1702        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
1703        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
1704        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
1705        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
1706
1707        ``dpop_jkt`` (RFC 9449 §10.1) binds the authorization code this push
1708        will produce to a DPoP key before the browser ever sees a redirect, so
1709        the code cannot be exchanged by whoever intercepts it. Pass the RFC
1710        7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key the token request will prove
1711        possession of; :func:`axiam_sdk._dpop.jwk_thumbprint_s256` computes it
1712        from a JWK. It is caller-supplied rather than derived because this SDK
1713        holds no DPoP key of its own (§21.9): it verifies proofs, it does not
1714        mint them. Omitted from the form entirely when ``None``.
1715
1716        Raises:
1717            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1718                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
1719            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
1720        """
1721        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1722        form = self._par_form(
1723            request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope, dpop_jkt=dpop_jkt
1724        )
1725        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
1726        http_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1727        response = self._rest_send_sync(http_request)
1728        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)
1729
1730    def oidc_exchange(
1731        self,
1732        *,
1733        code: str,
1734        code_verifier: SecretStr | str,
1735        redirect_uri: str,
1736        nonce: str,
1737        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1738        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1739    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1740        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=authorization_code``
1741        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — exchange an authorization code for a token
1742        set, validating the returned ID token in full before returning
1743        (§12.4). On ANY §12.4 failure the whole token set is discarded and
1744        ``AuthError`` is raised with the matching reason code (§12.4
1745        rule 7) — the access/refresh token from the same response is never
1746        returned."""
1747        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1748        form = self._exchange_form(
1749            code=code, code_verifier=code_verifier, redirect_uri=redirect_uri
1750        )
1751        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1752        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1753        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1754        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, nonce)
1755
1756    def oidc_refresh(
1757        self,
1758        *,
1759        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
1760        scope: str | None = None,
1761        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1762        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1763    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1764        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
1765        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
1766
1767        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
1768        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
1769        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
1770        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
1771        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
1772        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
1773        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
1774        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
1775        interleave.
1776        """
1777
1778        def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
1779            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
1780            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_sync`
1781            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
1782            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
1783            config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1784            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
1785            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1786            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1787            response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1788            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
1789            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1790
1791        def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
1792            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
1793            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
1794            :meth:`refresh` call."""
1795            token_set: OidcTokenSet = self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_sync(do_refresh)
1796            return token_set
1797
1798        result: OidcTokenSet = self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_sync.run(under_guard)
1799        return result
1800
1801    def login_client_credentials(
1802        self,
1803        *,
1804        scope: str | None = None,
1805        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1806        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1807    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1808        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=client_credentials``
1809        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — service-account machine-to-machine login.
1810        Requests no ``openid`` scope, so the response carries no
1811        ``id_token``.
1812
1813        Raises:
1814            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — this
1815                grant cannot be performed by a public client.
1816        """
1817        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1818        form = self._client_credentials_form(scope=scope)
1819        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1820        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1821        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1822        # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to this grant.
1823        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1824
1825    def device_authorize(
1826        self,
1827        *,
1828        scope: str | None = None,
1829        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1830        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1831    ) -> DeviceAuthorization:
1832        """``POST /oauth2/device_authorization`` (CONTRACT.md §14.1) — start
1833        the device grant and obtain the code pair.
1834
1835        **Unauthenticated by design.** A device that cannot show a browser
1836        also cannot hold a client secret, so this never sends
1837        ``client_secret`` and never refuses a client built without one.
1838
1839        Raises:
1840            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1841                ``device_authorization_endpoint``.
1842        """
1843        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1844        form = self._device_authorize_form(scope=scope)
1845        url = self._device_authorization_url(config, tenant_id)
1846        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1847        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1848        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
1849            raise error_from_oauth2_response(
1850                response.status_code, response, "device authorization request failed"
1851            )
1852        return self._build_device_authorization(response.json())
1853
1854    def device_poll(
1855        self,
1856        *,
1857        device_code: SecretStr | str,
1858        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1859        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1860    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1861        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the device-code grant (§14.1) — **one**
1862        poll attempt.
1863
1864        The raw single call, so an application driving its own loop (a UI
1865        rendering a countdown, say) can. The five RFC 8628 §3.5 answers
1866        surface as ``OAuthProtocolError`` — ``authorization_pending`` and
1867        ``slow_down`` included — so a hand-rolled loop sees exactly what
1868        :meth:`device_login` sees. Most callers want :meth:`device_login`.
1869        """
1870        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1871        form = self._device_poll_form(device_code=device_code)
1872        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1873        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1874        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1875        # No nonce: the device grant has no authorization request to carry one.
1876        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1877
1878    def device_login(
1879        self,
1880        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None],
1881        *,
1882        scope: str | None = None,
1883        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1884        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1885    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1886        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
1887        user code, poll to completion.
1888
1889        ``on_user_code`` is called with the :class:`DeviceAuthorization`
1890        **before the first poll** — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have
1891        had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK
1892        never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink
1893        panel) is the application's decision.
1894
1895        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
1896        set rather than adopting it, matching its ``login_client_credentials``
1897        posture.
1898
1899        Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response;
1900        ``slow_down`` adds 5 s **permanently**; ``authorization_pending``
1901        loops; ``access_denied`` and ``expired_token`` raise distinct errors;
1902        polling stops at ``expires_in`` even if the server has not yet said
1903        ``expired_token``. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is **not**
1904        terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by
1905        the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the
1906        user has already approved.
1907        """
1908        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1909        authorization = self.device_authorize(
1910            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
1911        )
1912
1913        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
1914        on_user_code(authorization)
1915
1916        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
1917        while True:
1918            if not schedule.tick():
1919                raise self._device_expired_error()
1920            time.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
1921            try:
1922                return self.device_poll(
1923                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
1924                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
1925                    configuration=config,
1926                )
1927            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
1928                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
1929                if outcome == "pending" or outcome == "retry":
1930                    continue
1931                if outcome == "slow_down":
1932                    schedule.slow_down()
1933                    continue
1934                raise
1935
1936    def token_exchange(
1937        self,
1938        *,
1939        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
1940        subject_token_type: str,
1941        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
1942        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
1943        audience: str | None = None,
1944        resource: str | None = None,
1945        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1946        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1947    ) -> ExchangedToken:
1948        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (CONTRACT.md §15.1)
1949        — exchange a token for a **narrower** one.
1950
1951        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1952
1953        * **No default ``actor_token``** (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for
1954          *impersonation*; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own
1955          session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
1956        * **No retry or downgrade on ``unauthorized_client``** (rule 2) — a
1957          registration fact an operator must fix.
1958        * **No auto-narrowing on ``invalid_scope``** (rule 3). The server
1959          refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds
1960          out here.
1961        * **No adoption** (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one
1962          outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every
1963          subsequent call this client makes.
1964
1965        A cross-tenant subject token answers ``invalid_grant``, identically to
1966        an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the
1967        server collapses them because distinguishing them is a
1968        tenant-enumeration signal.
1969
1970        Args:
1971            subject_token_type: What kind of token ``subject_token`` is.
1972                ``None`` sends :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE`, the
1973                same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a
1974                **trusted external issuer** (§15.7), set this explicitly —
1975                normally to :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE`. The SDK
1976                never reads ``subject_token`` to decide the value: which kind
1977                of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses
1978                refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry
1979                a refusal as a different type.
1980
1981        Raises:
1982            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1983                with no wire call.
1984        """
1985        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1986        form = self._token_exchange_form(
1987            subject_token=subject_token,
1988            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
1989            actor_token=actor_token,
1990            scopes=scopes,
1991            audience=audience,
1992            resource=resource,
1993        )
1994        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1995        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1996        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1997        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)
1998
1999    def uma_register_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource: ResourceSet) -> ResourceSet:
2000        """``POST /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — register a resource set
2001        (CONTRACT.md §20.1).
2002
2003        The returned ``id`` **is** the AXIAM resource id, directly usable as
2004        the ``resource_id`` of a later :meth:`uma_request_ticket`.

2010            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
2011        )
2012        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2013        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource registration failed")
2014        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

2057    def uma_list_resources(self, pat: SecretStr | str) -> list[str]:
2058        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — list the ids **this client**
2059        registered (§20.1).
2060
2061        Not the tenant's whole resource tree: a protection scope does not
2062        entitle a caller to enumerate it.

2073    def uma_request_ticket(
2074        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
2075    ) -> SecretStr:
2076        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
2077
2078        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
2079        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
2080        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
2081        server draws rather than flattening it.
2082        """
2083        body = [
2084            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
2085            for p in permissions
2086        ]
2087        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2088            "POST",
2089            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
2090            json=body,
2091            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
2092        )
2093        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2094        wire = cast(
2095            "dict[str, str]",
2096            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
2097        )
2098        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])
2099
2100    def uma_exchange_ticket(
2101        self,
2102        *,
2103        ticket: SecretStr | str,
2104        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
2105        tenant_id: str | None = None,
2106        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
2107    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
2108        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange
2109        a ticket for an RPT.
2110
2111        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
2112        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
2113        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
2114        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
2115        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the
2116        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
2117        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a
2118        **new** ticket.
2119
2120        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
2121
2122        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
2123          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
2124          resource server instead of for the user.
2125        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
2126          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
2127          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
2128        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
2129          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
2130          that user.
2131
2132        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
2133        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
2134        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
2135        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
2136
2137        Raises:
2138            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
2139                with no wire call.
2140        """
2141        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
2142        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
2143        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
2144        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
2145        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2146        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)
2147
2148    def logout_url(
2149        self,
2150        *,
2151        id_token: SecretStr | str,
2152        post_logout_redirect_uri: str | None = None,
2153        state: str | None = None,
2154        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
2155    ) -> str:
2156        """Build the RP-initiated logout URL to redirect the user agent to
2157        (CONTRACT.md §12.7.2).
2158
2159        Performs **no network I/O** beyond the discovery fetch the SDK caches
2160        anyway, and does **not** clear this client's own session: whether the
2161        local session ends is the application's decision — a backend holding a
2162        service-account session must not lose it because a *user* logged out.
2163
2164        ``end_session_endpoint`` is read from discovery and never synthesised
2165        from the issuer (rule 1). ``post_logout_redirect_uri`` is passed
2166        through unvalidated against any local list (rule 3): the allow-list
2167        lives in the client's server-side registration, and a client-side copy
2168        would drift and reject a URI an operator had just registered.
2169
2170        ``state`` is the caller's to generate and the caller's to check; the
2171        SDK never invents one, because the value only means something to the
2172        application that will receive it back.
2173        """
2174        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
2175        return self._logout_url_impl(
2176            config,
2177            id_token=id_token,
2178            post_logout_redirect_uri=post_logout_redirect_uri,
2179            state=state,
2180        )
2181
2182    def verify_logout_token(
2183        self,
2184        token: str,
2185        *,
2186        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
2187    ) -> VerifiedLogoutToken:
2188        """Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this
2189        application's ``backchannel_logout_uri`` (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).
2190
2191        Every check exists because skipping it has a name:
2192
2193        1. **Signature**, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token
2194           path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same
2195           ``kid``-required discipline.
2196        2. **``iss``/``aud``**: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
2197        3. **``events`` carries the back-channel-logout key.** This is what
2198           distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means
2199           accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
2200        4. **``nonce`` is absent.** Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it,
2201           and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being
2202           replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
2203        5. **At least one of ``sid``/``sub``** — a token naming neither
2204           identifies nothing.
2205        6. **``exp`` in the future, ``iat`` recent.**
2206
2207        Returns:
2208            The ``sid``/``sub``/``jti`` the token names — never a bare
2209            ``bool``, because the RP has to know *which* session to end.
2210            **Dedup on ``jti`` yourself**: delivery is at-least-once, so a
2211            valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard
2212            would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second
2213            logout after a restart.
2214        """
2215        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
2216        return self._verify_logout_token_impl(token, config)
2217

2297    def sso_providers(
2298        self,
2299        *,
2300        org_id: str | None = None,
2301        org_slug: str | None = None,
2302        tenant_id: str | None = None,

2305        """``GET /api/v1/auth/federation/providers`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
2306        which "Sign in with X" buttons to render for a workspace.

2308        The identifiers travel as **query** parameters; this is a ``GET``
2309        and sends no body.
2310
2311        **An empty list is a success.** An unknown organization, a known one
2312        with nothing configured, and a request naming no workspace at all
2313        all answer ``200`` with an empty ``providers`` array (§12.1 note 9).
2314        Every one of them comes back as an ordinary result, and nothing here
2315        synthesises a not-found: the endpoint is deliberately shaped so it
2316        cannot be used to enumerate organization or tenant slugs, and an SDK
2317        that reintroduced the distinction would reintroduce the oracle. A
2318        caller learns it named the workspace wrongly at the start
2319        operations, where every failure is a uniform ``401``.

2321        For the same reason this is the one federation operation that does
2322        **not** refuse client-side when no workspace resolves.

2325            org_id=org_id,
2326            org_slug=org_slug,
2327            tenant_id=tenant_id,
2328            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
2329        )
2330        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("GET", SSO_PROVIDERS_PATH, params=params)
2331        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2332        return self._handle_sso_providers_response(response)
