2334    def sso_start_oauth2(
2335        self,
2336        *,
2337        federation_config_id: str,
2338        redirect_uri: str,
2339        tenant_id: str | None = None,
2340        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
2341        org_id: str | None = None,
2342        org_slug: str | None = None,
2343    ) -> SsoStartResult:
2344        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/start`` (CONTRACT.md
2345        §12.1) — step 1 of a login through a **plain-OAuth2** upstream
2346        (GitHub, Facebook, ``generic_oauth2``).
2347
2348        Call this, rather than :meth:`sso_start`, exactly when the
2349        provider's ``protocol`` is ``OAuth2`` (§12.1 note 10). The server
2350        refuses a mismatch with ``400`` rather than accepting it silently,
2351        so a client that assumes OIDC fails on every GitHub button.
2352
2353        PKCE is mandatory on this path and is generated and stored
2354        **server-side**; nothing about it appears in the request or the
2355        response (§12.1 note 11).
2356
2357        A ``400`` here can mean the ``redirect_uri`` is not on an origin the
2358        deployment accepts (§12.1 rule 12a); it surfaces as
2359        :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` and is not retried.
2360        """
2361        body = self._sso_start_oauth2_body(
2362            federation_config_id=federation_config_id,
2363            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
2364            tenant_id=tenant_id,
2365            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
2366            org_id=org_id,
2367            org_slug=org_slug,
2368        )
2369        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", SSO_OAUTH2_START_PATH, json=body)
2370        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2371        return self._handle_sso_start_oauth2_response(response)
2372
2373    def sso_complete_oauth2(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
2374        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/callback`` (CONTRACT.md
2375        §12.1) — step 2 of a plain-OAuth2 login.
2376
2377        The session arrives as ``Set-Cookie`` (§12.1 note 6) and is absorbed
2378        exactly as :meth:`sso_complete` absorbs it, so ``refresh()`` and
2379        ``logout()`` work afterwards.
2380
2381        §12.4 does not apply: an ``OAuth2`` provider issues no ID token, so
2382        there is nothing to validate. The server authenticated the user by
2383        calling a configured userinfo endpoint with the access token it had
2384        just received — configuration and transport trust rather than
2385        cryptographic trust (§12.1 note 11).
2386        """
2387        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2388            "POST", SSO_OAUTH2_CALLBACK_PATH, json={"state": state, "code": code}
2389        )
2390        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2391        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteOauth2")
2392
2393    def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
2394        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/handoff`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
2395        redeem the single-use code the SAML and Apple flows deliver.
2396
2397        Those two protocols return **cross-site**, so the server cannot set
2398        ``SameSite=Strict`` session cookies on that response. It instead
2399        redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an
2400        ``axiam_handoff`` query parameter (``HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM``); this
2401        call posts that code back same-origin, and *this* response is the
2402        one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).
2403
2404        **The code is gone either way.** It is valid for
2405        ``HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`` seconds and redeemable **once**. Redeem
2406        it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed
2407        redemption: a ``401`` is terminal, and this method makes exactly one
2408        wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown,
2409        expired and already-redeemed all answer the same ``401``,
2410        deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to
2411        do.
2412        """
2413        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2414            "POST", SSO_HANDOFF_PATH, json={"code": code}
2415        )
2416        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2417        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteHandoff")
2418
2419    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
2420    # §24 WebAuthn / passkeys — the relying-party layer
2421    #
2422    # Python has no authenticator, so §24.6b's linked-API helper is
2423    # deliberately absent: §24.6b rule 2 forbids emulating one in software,
2424    # and a "credential" held in process memory is not a second factor. What
2425    # is here is the half that talks to AXIAM, plus §24.6a's JSON bridge —
2426    # which is what lets a Python service be the relying party for a ceremony
2427    # a handset ran.
2428    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
2429
2430    def webauthn_register_start(self) -> WebauthnChallenge:
2431        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
2432
2433        Requires a session — enrolling a passkey is something a signed-in user
2434        does to their own account — and refuses **client-side with no wire
2435        call** when there is none.
2436
2437        A ``503`` means the tenant's attestation policy requires attestation
2438        and the FIDO metadata service has no usable snapshot. That is a server
2439        configuration state, not a transient failure, so §24.4 rule 2
2440        deliberately does **not** retry it.
2441        """
2442        self._ensure_open()
2443        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_start")
2444        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", self._WA_REGISTER_START, json={})
2445        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2446        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_register_start")
2447
2448    def webauthn_register_finish(
2449        self,
2450        *,
2451        state_token: SecretStr | str,
2452        credential_name: str,
2453        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
2454    ) -> WebauthnCredential:
2455        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
2456
2457        ``response`` is either the parsed authenticator answer or the
2458        platform's own JSON string (§24.6a rule 2) — Android's
2459        ``registrationResponseJson``, a browser's ``credential.toJSON()``. It
2460        reaches the server unchanged either way: it is the input to a
2461        signature check over bytes this SDK did not produce.
2462        """
2463        self._ensure_open()
2464        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_finish")
2465        body = self._webauthn_register_finish_body(state_token, credential_name, response)
2466        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2467            "POST", self._WA_REGISTER_FINISH, json=body
2468        )
2469        return self._webauthn_credential(self._rest_send_sync(request))
2470
2471    def webauthn_authenticate_start(self, *, challenge_token: SecretStr | str) -> WebauthnChallenge:
2472        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
2473
2474        The **second-factor** ceremony: it continues a ``login()`` that
2475        answered ``mfa_required`` with ``"webauthn"`` among its methods, and
2476        ``challenge_token`` is that result's ``mfa_token``.
2477
2478        A different flow from :meth:`webauthn_discoverable_start`, not the same
2479        one with an optional argument — see §24.2 for why they cannot be
2480        merged.
2481        """
2482        self._ensure_open()
2483        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2484            "POST", self._WA_AUTH_START, json={"challenge_token": _expose_token(challenge_token)}
2485        )
2486        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2487        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_authenticate_start")
2488
2489    def webauthn_authenticate_finish(
2490        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
2491    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
2492        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
2493
2494        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3 rule 1). That is not §14.3's
2495        "MAY adopt" posture: ``device_login`` mints tokens a caller may want to
2496        route elsewhere, and this is the SDK's own primary authentication —
2497        returning a token set without adopting it would make a passkey sign-in
2498        the one way to log in that does not log you in.
2499        """
2500        return self._webauthn_finish_sync(
2501            self._WA_AUTH_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_authenticate_finish"
2502        )
2503
2504    def webauthn_discoverable_start(
2505        self, *, workspace: WebauthnWorkspace | None = None
2506    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
2507        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
2508
2509        The **primary-factor** ceremony: nothing precedes it, the server sends
2510        an empty ``allowCredentials``, and the assertion itself identifies the
2511        user. The workspace still has to be named — a discoverable credential
2512        is resolved inside one tenant — but it comes from this client's own
2513        configuration unless overridden, and slugs are accepted.
2514        """
2515        self._ensure_open()
2516        body = self._webauthn_discoverable_body(workspace)
2517        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2518            "POST", self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_START, json=body
2519        )
2520        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2521        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_discoverable_start")
2522
2523    def webauthn_discoverable_finish(
2524        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
2525    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
2526        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
2527
2528        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3). Unlike its username-bound
2529        twin, this fires the server's ``login.post_auth`` reactor hook (§22.5):
2530        there was no password step for the event to have been fired at.
2531        """
2532        return self._webauthn_finish_sync(
2533            self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_discoverable_finish"
2534        )
2535
2536    def _webauthn_finish_sync(
2537        self,
2538        path: str,
2539        state_token: SecretStr | str,
2540        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
2541        operation: str,
2542    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
2543        """The shared tail of both authentication ceremonies."""
2544        self._ensure_open()
2545        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
2546        # this call changes the subject.
2547        self._on_credential_change()
2548        body = self._webauthn_finish_body(state_token, response, operation)
2549        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
2550        http_response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2551        result = self._webauthn_login_result(http_response, operation)
2552        # The server sets the same axiam_access/axiam_refresh/axiam_csrf triple
2553        # here as it does on a password login, so adoption is the same call.
2554        self._absorb_session_cookies()
2555        return result
2556
2557    def webauthn_setup_register_start(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str) -> WebauthnChallenge:
2558        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/setup/register/start`` (CONTRACT.md
2559        §24.1, §25.2 rule 2 — contract 1.45).
2560
2561        Enrols a passkey or security key as the account's **first** factor
2562        during the forced enrolment ``login()`` demanded — the WebAuthn twin
2563        of :meth:`mfa_setup_enroll`. Takes **no session**: the setup token
2564        from ``login()``'s ``mfa_setup_required`` outcome is the only
2565        credential, and it travels in the body. Unlike
2566        :meth:`webauthn_register_start`, this does **not** call the
2567        require-session guard and does **not** attach this client's own
2568        session credential — even one already configured (§24.8).
2569        """
2570        self._ensure_open()
2571        request = self._session._credential_free_request(
2572            "POST",
2573            self._WA_SETUP_REGISTER_START,
2574            self._webauthn_setup_register_start_body(setup_token),
2575        )
2576        response = self._session._send_sync_credential_free(request)
2577        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_setup_register_start")
2578
2579    def webauthn_setup_register_finish(
2580        self,
2581        *,
2582        setup_token: SecretStr | str,
2583        state_token: SecretStr | str,
2584        credential_name: str,
2585        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
2586    ) -> LoginResult:
2587        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/setup/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md
2588        §24.1, §25.2 rule 2 — contract 1.45).
2589
2590        Completes the login ``login()`` interrupted, exactly as
2591        :meth:`mfa_setup_confirm` does for TOTP: adopts credentials on success
2592        (§24.3's five rules apply verbatim, per §25.2 rule 2) and clears the
2593        §17 decision memo because the subject changed. Takes no session, for
2594        the same reason :meth:`webauthn_setup_register_start` does not — a
2595        second credential on a call whose only credential is meant to be the
2596        setup token invites a server that changes its mind about which to
2597        trust.
2598
2599        A ``403`` here is the tenant's attestation policy refusing **this
2600        authenticator** — an AAGUID that is not allow-listed, a missing FIDO
2601        certification, a revoked status — and its message is surfaced
2602        verbatim (§24.4 rule 1): it is the only way the person holding the
2603        key learns that a different one would work.
2604        """
2605        self._ensure_open()
2606        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
2607        # this call changes the subject.
2608        self._on_credential_change()
2609        body = self._webauthn_setup_register_finish_body(
2610            setup_token, state_token, credential_name, response
2611        )
2612        request = self._session._credential_free_request(
2613            "POST", self._WA_SETUP_REGISTER_FINISH, body
2614        )
2615        http_response = self._session._send_sync_credential_free(request)
2616        return self._handle_setup_register_finish_response(http_response)
2617
2618    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
2619    # §25 Account lifecycle and MFA enrolment
2620    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
2621
2622    def mfa_enroll(self) -> MfaEnrollment:
2623        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
2624        voluntary TOTP enrolment for the signed-in user.
2625
2626        Changes nothing about the current session. In particular it does
2627        **not** clear the §17 decision memo: the subject has not changed, and
2628        discarding a warm memo on an unrelated profile action costs a round
2629        trip on every check that follows (§25.2 rule 3).
2630        """
2631        self._ensure_open()
2632        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_MFA_ENROLL, json={})
2633        return self._mfa_enrollment(self._rest_send_sync(request), "mfa_enroll")
2634
2635    def mfa_confirm(self, *, totp_code: str) -> bool:
2636        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — activate the
2637        factor :meth:`mfa_enroll` offered."""
2638        self._ensure_open()
2639        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2640            "POST", self._AC_MFA_CONFIRM, json={"totp_code": totp_code}
2641        )
2642        return self._mfa_confirmed(self._rest_send_sync(request))
2643
2644    def mfa_setup_enroll(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str) -> MfaEnrollment:
2645        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
2646        the enrolment a ``login()`` demanded.
2647
2648        Reached when ``login()`` returns ``mfa_setup_required``: the tenant
2649        requires MFA and this account has none. There is no session yet — the
2650        setup token *is* the credential.
2651        """
2652        self._ensure_open()
2653        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2654            "POST", self._AC_MFA_SETUP_ENROLL, json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token)}
2655        )
2656        return self._mfa_enrollment(self._rest_send_sync(request), "mfa_setup_enroll")
2657
2658    def mfa_setup_confirm(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str, totp_code: str) -> LoginResult:
2659        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — finish
2660        forced enrolment and, with it, the login that was interrupted.
2661
2662        Adopts credentials exactly as ``login()`` does, because it *is* the
2663        completion of a login (§25.2 rule 2).
2664        """
2665        self._ensure_open()
2666        self._on_credential_change()
2667        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2668            "POST",
2669            self._AC_MFA_SETUP_CONFIRM,
2670            json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token), "totp_code": totp_code},
2671        )
2672        return self._handle_login_response(self._rest_send_sync(request))

2674    def verify_email(self, *, token: SecretStr | str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
2675        """``POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1).
2676
2677        Unauthenticated: a user whose address is unverified may have no session
2678        at all. ``tenant_id`` is a **body** field here — this is not an
2679        ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint, so §12.1 rule 2's query-parameter convention
2680        does not reach it.
2681        """
2682        self._ensure_open()
2683        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2684            "POST",
2685            self._AC_VERIFY_EMAIL,
2686            json={"token": _expose_token(token), "tenant_id": tenant_id},
2687        )
2688        self._expect_no_content(self._rest_send_sync(request), "verify_email")
2689
2690    def resend_verification(self, *, email: str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
2691        """``POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the
2692        **unauthenticated** resend, for a caller with no session.
2693
2694        **Returns normally whatever the outcome.** The address may not exist,
2695        may already be verified, or may be over the daily limit, and this
2696        answers identically in all of them, because it takes an address from an
2697        anonymous caller and anything else is an oracle for which addresses have
2698        accounts (§25.7).
2699
2700        A caller that *is* signed in wants :meth:`resend_own_verification`,
2701        which says which of those happened. Do not reach for this one because it
2702        is the name you already knew.
2703        """
2704        self._ensure_open()
2705        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2706            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_VERIFICATION, json={"email": email, "tenant_id": tenant_id}
2707        )
2708        self._expect_no_content(self._rest_send_sync(request), "resend_verification")
2709
2710    def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
2711        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
2712        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
2713        and say what happened.
2714
2715        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
2716        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
2717        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
2718        address.
2719
2720        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
2721        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
2722        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
2723
2724        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
2725          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
2726          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
2727          succeeding.
2728        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
2729          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
2730        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
2731
2732        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
2733        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
2734        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
2735        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
2736        """
2737        self._ensure_open()
2738        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2739            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
2740        )
2741        self._expect_no_content(self._rest_send_sync(request), "resend_own_verification")
2742
2743    def request_password_reset(
2744        self,
2745        *,
2746        email: str,
2747        org_slug: str | None = None,
2748        tenant_id: str | None = None,
2749        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
2750    ) -> None:
2751        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — ask for a reset
2752        mail.
2753
2754        **Returns normally whether or not the address exists**, and this SDK
2755        exposes no way to tell the two apart. That is not an omission to
2756        improve on: a client that surfaced a "no such user" state — even one
2757        inferred from timing — would turn the endpoint into the account
2758        enumeration oracle its uniform response exists to prevent (§25.4).
2759        """
2760        self._ensure_open()
2761        body = self._password_reset_body(
2762            email=email, org_slug=org_slug, tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_slug=tenant_slug
2763        )
2764        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_RESET, json=body)
2765        self._expect_no_content(self._rest_send_sync(request), "request_password_reset")
2766
2767    def password_reset_context(self, *, token: SecretStr | str) -> PasswordResetContext:
2768        """``GET /api/v1/auth/reset/context`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the OPAQUE
2769        policy for the account a reset token belongs to.
2770
2771        Call this before :meth:`confirm_password_reset` on any tenant that
2772        might have §23 enabled: the client has to build a registration record,
2773        and building one needs parameters it cannot know before it has a token
2774        to ask with. Sending a plaintext password to a tenant in
2775        ``opaque_mode: required`` is refused, and refused late (§25.4 rule 1).

2779            "GET", self._AC_RESET_CONTEXT, params={"token": _expose_token(token)}
2780        )
2781        return self._reset_context(self._rest_send_sync(request))

2784        self,

The AXIAM SDK's sync REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10).

client.login(...) returns a typed ~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult with mfa_required (SC#1). For the async twin, use ~axiam_sdk.AsyncAxiamClient (SDK-Q08) — a separate class, not an async_* method on this one.

def close(self) -> None: 
1127    def close(self) -> None:
1128        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
1129
1130        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
1131        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
1132
1133        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
1134        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
1135        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
1136        restart and resume; a ``close()`` that logged out would silently end
1137        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
1138        ending the session is what you want.
1139
1140        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
1141        rather than silently reconnecting.
1142        """
1143        self._closed = True
1144        self._decision_memo.clear()
1145        self._session.close()

Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).

Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.

This does not log out. §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases local resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process restart and resume; a close() that logged out would silently end every user's session on each deploy. Call logout() first if ending the session is what you want.

After this returns, any operation on the client raises NetworkError rather than silently reconnecting.

1151    def acting_tenant(self, tenant_id: str) -> AxiamClient:
1152        """A handle to this client that acts on ``tenant_id`` — CONTRACT.md
1153        §5.2 rule 1 (contract 1.51).
1154
1155        The returned handle shares everything with ``self`` — session,
1156        cookie jar, refresh guard, telemetry, decision memo — and differs
1157        only in the ``X-Axiam-Tenant`` it sends. ``self`` is unchanged, so
1158        two tasks can act on two tenants at once over one session. Call
1159        :meth:`clear_acting_tenant` on the returned handle (or on ``self``)
1160        to act on the principal's own tenant again.
1161
1162        Meaningful only for an **organization-level** principal; see the
1163        ``acting_tenant`` constructor parameter for what the header does and
1164        does not reach (not ``X-Tenant-ID``, not a ``{tenant_id}`` path, not
1165        gRPC).
1166
1167        Raises:
1168            NetworkError: if ``tenant_id`` is not a UUID.
1169            AuthzError: when this client holds a login result that reported
1170                the principal's reach: if it reported
1171                ``organization_level: False`` (an ordinary tenant principal
1172                is a principal of one tenant, and the server answers ``403``
1173                to anything else), or if it reported ``reachable_tenant_ids``
1174                that does not contain ``tenant_id`` (§5.2.3 rule 4). A client
1175                holding no such result — a service account from client
1176                credentials or the device login, an injected token, a
1177                session completed without a user object — has nothing to
1178                gate on, so the handle is returned and the server's ``403``
1179                is the answer. An organization-level **service account** is
1180                a supported design, and the server honours the header for
1181                one on the terms it does for a user.
1182
1183        There is no string-vs-UUID ambiguity to resolve: the server silently
1184        ignores a value that is not a UUID and answers for the caller's own
1185        tenant instead, so refusing a non-UUID client-side is the refusal.
1186        """
1187        normalized = self._check_acting_tenant_gate(tenant_id)
1188        handle = copy.copy(self)
1189        handle._acting_tenant = normalized
1190        return handle

A handle to this client that acts on tenant_id — CONTRACT.md §5.2 rule 1 (contract 1.51).

The returned handle shares everything with self — session, cookie jar, refresh guard, telemetry, decision memo — and differs only in the X-Axiam-Tenant it sends. self is unchanged, so two tasks can act on two tenants at once over one session. Call clear_acting_tenant() on the returned handle (or on self) to act on the principal's own tenant again.

Meaningful only for an organization-level principal; see the acting_tenant constructor parameter for what the header does and does not reach (not X-Tenant-ID, not a {tenant_id} path, not gRPC).

Raises: NetworkError: if tenant_id is not a UUID. AuthzError: when this client holds a login result that reported the principal's reach: if it reported organization_level: False (an ordinary tenant principal is a principal of one tenant, and the server answers 403 to anything else), or if it reported reachable_tenant_ids that does not contain tenant_id (§5.2.3 rule 4). A client holding no such result — a service account from client credentials or the device login, an injected token, a session completed without a user object — has nothing to gate on, so the handle is returned and the server's 403 is the answer. An organization-level service account is a supported design, and the server honours the header for one on the terms it does for a user.

There is no string-vs-UUID ambiguity to resolve: the server silently ignores a value that is not a UUID and answers for the caller's own tenant instead, so refusing a non-UUID client-side is the refusal.

def clear_acting_tenant(self) -> AxiamClient:

1193        """A handle to this client that sends **no** ``X-Axiam-Tenant`` — the

1196        :meth:`acting_tenant`."""

1198        handle._acting_tenant = None

def authenticate_device(self) -> DeviceToken: 
1205    def authenticate_device(self) -> DeviceToken:
1206        """``POST /api/v1/auth/device`` (CONTRACT.md §6.1) — the mTLS device
1207        login. No request body; returns a typed :class:`DeviceToken` and
1208        adopts ``access_token`` as this client's credential, exactly as a
1209        successful :meth:`login` is adopted.
1210
1211        **Reachable only on a client configured with a client certificate**
1212        (``client_cert``/``client_key`` — see the constructor). Without one
1213        the server would answer ``401`` regardless, so this refuses
1214        client-side instead, with zero wire calls (rule 7).
1215
1216        There is **no refresh token** (D-6 of the dogfooding remediation
1217        plan): a later ``401`` on this credential is surfaced as
1218        :class:`~axiam_sdk.AuthError` without a refresh attempt — call this
1219        method again, which costs one TLS handshake.
1220
1221        Raises:
1222            AuthError: with zero wire calls, if this client was not built
1223                with a client certificate (rule 7); or, from the server,
1224                for an unknown, untrusted, expired, revoked or unbound
1225                certificate, or a ``Server``-type certificate (rule 8 — every
1226                refusal is a ``401``, surfaced with the server's own message).
1227            NetworkError: for a ``429`` (rate-limited; not an authentication
1228                failure, rule 8) or any other transport/status failure.
1229        """
1230        self._ensure_open()
1231        self._reachable_only_with_client_cert("authenticate_device")
1232        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", DEVICE_AUTH_PATH)
1233        # This call is itself a login: withhold the jar explicitly, rather
1234        # than relying on _apply_bearer_credential, which only overrides
1235        # Cookie once a bearer token is already held — never true on the
1236        # very call that is about to mint one. Without this, a cookie left
1237        # by an earlier login() on this client rides along on the request
1238        # that is supposed to authenticate as the device alone, and the
1239        # server reads axiam_access before Authorization (CONTRACT.md §6.1).
1240        request.headers["Cookie"] = ""
1241        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1242        return self._handle_device_auth_response(response)

Reachable only on a client configured with a client certificate (client_cert/client_key — see the constructor). Without one the server would answer 401 regardless, so this refuses client-side instead, with zero wire calls (rule 7).

There is no refresh token (D-6 of the dogfooding remediation plan): a later 401 on this credential is surfaced as ~axiam_sdk.AuthError without a refresh attempt — call this method again, which costs one TLS handshake.

Raises: AuthError: with zero wire calls, if this client was not built with a client certificate (rule 7); or, from the server, for an unknown, untrusted, expired, revoked or unbound certificate, or a Server-type certificate (rule 8 — every refusal is a 401, surfaced with the server's own message). NetworkError: for a 429 (rate-limited; not an authentication failure, rule 8) or any other transport/status failure.

def login_opaque( self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult: 
1260    def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
1261        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
1262
1263        Returns the same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
1264        ``mfa_required`` case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.
1265
1266        What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither
1267        useful without the account's registration record **and** the tenant's
1268        OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request
1269        log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password,
1270        because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database
1271        is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not
1272        offer. It does **not** protect against a compromised AXIAM server.
1273
1274        Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server
1275        proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the
1276        server during the handshake, so opening ``KE2`` *is* the proof that it
1277        holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an ``M2`` check in
1278        capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now
1279        nothing to skip.
1280
1281        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
1282            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
1283            SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not ``AuthError``: reporting a
1284            configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to
1285            reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to
1286            :meth:`login`.
1287        :raises AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist,
1288            an account with no registration record, and a server that does not
1289            hold the record — indistinguishable by design. **Nothing is sent to
1290            ``login/finish`` in that case** (§23.4 rule 7).
1291
1292        **The ``mode`` field decides what happens after a failed exchange**, and
1293        nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). ``login/start`` carries the tenant's
1294        ``opaque_mode``:
1295
1296        * ``"optional"`` — this method retries over :meth:`login` with the same
1297          credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's
1298          outcome. Under ``optional`` an account with no record is the ordinary
1299          case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an
1300          operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a
1301          password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every
1302          user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state ``optional`` exists
1303          to serve.
1304        * ``"required"``, an unrecognised value, or **no ``mode`` at all** (a
1305          server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is
1306          retried over :meth:`login`. It would be refused anyway: ``required``
1307          answers ``403 opaque_required`` for every principal in the tenant, so
1308          trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.
1309
1310        ``mode`` is **not** downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a
1311        hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer ``404`` and get
1312        the fallback whatever it puts here. ``required`` is what closes that,
1313        server-side, by refusing ``/auth/login`` before examining any
1314        credential.
1315
1316        This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by
1317        default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is
1318        the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by
1319        someone holding the OPRF seed.
1320        """
1321        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
1322
1323        self._ensure_open()
1324        self._on_credential_change()
1325
1326        exchange = start_login(password)
1327
1328        # One round trip, always. SRP had to guess a group before the server
1329        # named one and restart the exchange if it guessed wrong; ``KE1`` does
1330        # not depend on the KSF.
1331        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1332            "POST",
1333            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
1334            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
1335        )
1336        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1337        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
1338            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
1339        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
1340
1341        try:
1342            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
1343        except AuthError:
1344            # §23.4 rule 7. `KE3` is not sent either way; `mode` — and only
1345            # `mode` — decides whether the plaintext path may be tried.
1346            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
1347                raise
1348            return self.login(username_or_email, password)
1349
1350        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1351            "POST",
1352            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
1353            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
1354        )
1355        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1356        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
1357            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
1358        return self._handle_login_response(response)

OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.

Returns the same LoginResult as login(), including the mfa_required case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.

What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither useful without the account's registration record and the tenant's OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password, because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not offer. It does not protect against a compromised AXIAM server.

Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the server during the handshake, so opening KE2 is the proof that it holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an M2 check in capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now nothing to skip.

Raises
  • NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not AuthError: reporting a configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to login().
  • AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist, an account with no registration record, and a server that does not hold the record — indistinguishable by design. Nothing is sent to login/finish in that case (§23.4 rule 7).

The mode field decides what happens after a failed exchange, and nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). login/start carries the tenant's opaque_mode:

  • "optional" — this method retries over login() with the same credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's outcome. Under optional an account with no record is the ordinary case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state optional exists to serve.
  • "required", an unrecognised value, or no mode at all (a server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is retried over login(). It would be refused anyway: required answers 403 opaque_required for every principal in the tenant, so trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.

mode is not downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer 404 and get the fallback whatever it puts here. required is what closes that, server-side, by refusing /auth/login before examining any credential.

This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by someone holding the OPRF seed.

1360    def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1361        """Build a registration record sealed against the tenant this client is
1362        **acting on**.
1363

1365        in it — §27 ``users.create``, and the reset-completion flow, which names
1366        its own tenant. It is the **wrong** tenant for the caller's own password
1367        change once an organization-level principal has selected another one to
1368        act on: the account's credentials live where the account does. Use
1369        :meth:`opaque_enrollment_for_self` there — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2.
1370
1371        The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to
1372        arrive with the request or not at all.
1373
1374        Performs a ``register/start`` round trip, which the SRP verifier this
1375        replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's
1376        oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid
1377        record.
1378

1380        the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a
1381        verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential
1382        identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.
1383
1384        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
1385            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
1386            SDK cannot perform.
1387        """
1388        return self._enroll(password, None)

That is the right tenant when the record is for an account being created in it — §27 users.create, and the reset-completion flow, which names its own tenant. It is the wrong tenant for the caller's own password change once an organization-level principal has selected another one to act on: the account's credentials live where the account does. Use opaque_enrollment_for_self() there — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2.

The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to arrive with the request or not at all.

Performs a register/start round trip, which the SRP verifier this replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid record.

Note the absence of an identity argument. The SRP version required the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.

def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, typing.Any]: 
1390    def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1391        """Build a registration record for the **caller's own** new password,
1392        sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.
1393
1394        CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2. ``POST /auth/password/change`` and the record
1395        that accompanies it are about the account, not about whatever tenant the
1396        client is currently pointed at, and a record sealed against the acting
1397        tenant is refused with *"the OPAQUE session was issued for a different
1398        tenant"*.
1399
1400        The distinction only bites for an organization-level principal that has
1401        selected another tenant to act on; for everyone else the two tenants are
1402        the same value and this behaves identically to
1403        :meth:`opaque_enrollment`. It is still the method to call for a
1404        self-service password change, because which principal is signed in is
1405        not something the call site usually knows.
1406
1407        :raises NetworkError: when no login has completed on this client yet —
1408            the principal tenant is reported by the login response, so there is
1409            nothing to seal against before then — and on the same terms as
1410            :meth:`opaque_enrollment` otherwise.
1411        """
1412        if self._principal_tenant_id is None:
1413            raise NetworkError(
1414                "OPAQUE: no principal tenant is known yet — sign in before "
1415                "building a registration record for your own password"
1416            )
1417        return self._enroll(password, self._principal_tenant_id)

Build a registration record for the caller's own new password, sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.

CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2. POST /auth/password/change and the record that accompanies it are about the account, not about whatever tenant the client is currently pointed at, and a record sealed against the acting tenant is refused with "the OPAQUE session was issued for a different tenant".

The distinction only bites for an organization-level principal that has selected another tenant to act on; for everyone else the two tenants are the same value and this behaves identically to opaque_enrollment(). It is still the method to call for a self-service password change, because which principal is signed in is not something the call site usually knows.

Raises
  • NetworkError: when no login has completed on this client yet — the principal tenant is reported by the login response, so there is nothing to seal against before then — and on the same terms as opaque_enrollment() otherwise.

1460    def refresh(self) -> None:
1461        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
1462        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
1463        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
1464        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""

1466        self._on_credential_change()
1467        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)

1470
1471        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
1472        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
1473        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
1474        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
1475        self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_sync(
1476            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_sync(tenant_id, org_id)
1477        )

def check_access( self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None, *, subject_id: str | None = None) -> AccessResult: 
1520    def check_access(
1521        self,
1522        action: str,
1523        resource_id: str,
1524        scope: str | None = None,
1525        *,
1526        subject_id: str | None = None,
1527    ) -> AccessResult:
1528        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
1529
1530        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
1531        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
1532        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
1533        declarative ``require_access`` helpers (§11) pass to check the
1534        *request's* authenticated user.
1535        """
1536        self._ensure_open()
1537        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
1538        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
1539        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id, self._acting_tenant)
1540        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
1541        if memoized is not None:
1542            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
1543            return memoized
1544
1545        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
1546        wire = self._authz_post_sync(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
1547        result = AccessResult(**wire)
1548
1549        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
1550        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
1551        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
1552        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
1553        return result

def oidc_par( self, *, request: AuthorizationRequest, redirect_uri: str, scope: str | list[str] | None = None, dpop_jkt: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest: 
1674    def oidc_par(
1675        self,
1676        *,
1677        request: AuthorizationRequest,
1678        redirect_uri: str,
1679        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1680        dpop_jkt: str | None = None,
1681        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1682        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1683    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
1684        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
1685        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
1686        with.
1687
1688        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
1689        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
1690        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
1691        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
1692        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
1693        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
1694
1695        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
1696        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
1697        authorize any other way (§21.1).
1698
1699        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
1700        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
1701
1702        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
1703        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
1704        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
1705        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
1706
1707        ``dpop_jkt`` (RFC 9449 §10.1) binds the authorization code this push
1708        will produce to a DPoP key before the browser ever sees a redirect, so
1709        the code cannot be exchanged by whoever intercepts it. Pass the RFC
1710        7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key the token request will prove
1711        possession of; :func:`axiam_sdk._dpop.jwk_thumbprint_s256` computes it
1712        from a JWK. It is caller-supplied rather than derived because this SDK
1713        holds no DPoP key of its own (§21.9): it verifies proofs, it does not
1714        mint them. Omitted from the form entirely when ``None``.
1715
1716        Raises:
1717            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1718                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
1719            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
1720        """
1721        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1722        form = self._par_form(
1723            request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope, dpop_jkt=dpop_jkt
1724        )
1725        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
1726        http_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1727        response = self._rest_send_sync(http_request)
1728        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)

POST /oauth2/par (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect with.

PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting scope, redirect_uri, state and the PKCE challenge into a URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque request_uri in the redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that cannot be edited into meaning something else.

Required for a FAPI 2.0 client — profile: "fapi2" refuses a registration that does not set require_par, so such a client cannot authorize any other way (§21.1).

A §12 extension, not a replacement: oidc_exchange afterwards is unchanged, and takes the code_verifier carried on the result.

Not retried on a 5xx or a transport failure — it is a POST that creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only eligibility exactly as oidc_exchange does. The safe recovery is a fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).

dpop_jkt (RFC 9449 §10.1) binds the authorization code this push will produce to a DPoP key before the browser ever sees a redirect, so the code cannot be exchanged by whoever intercepts it. Pass the RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key the token request will prove possession of; axiam_sdk._dpop.jwk_thumbprint_s256() computes it from a JWK. It is caller-supplied rather than derived because this SDK holds no DPoP key of its own (§21.9): it verifies proofs, it does not mint them. Omitted from the form entirely when None.

Raises: AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint. OAuthProtocolError: on any error the server returns.

def oidc_refresh( self, *, refresh_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
1756    def oidc_refresh(
1757        self,
1758        *,
1759        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
1760        scope: str | None = None,
1761        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1762        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1763    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1764        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
1765        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
1766
1767        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
1768        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
1769        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
1770        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
1771        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
1772        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
1773        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
1774        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
1775        interleave.
1776        """
1777
1778        def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
1779            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
1780            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_sync`
1781            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
1782            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
1783            config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1784            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
1785            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1786            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1787            response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1788            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
1789            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1790
1791        def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
1792            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
1793            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
1794            :meth:`refresh` call."""
1795            token_set: OidcTokenSet = self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_sync(do_refresh)
1796            return token_set
1797
1798        result: OidcTokenSet = self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_sync.run(under_guard)
1799        return result

POST /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an OidcTokenSet.

A distinct operation from refresh(), which drives the cookie/opaque-token session path at POST /api/v1/auth/refresh (§12.1 "oidc_refresh vs refresh") — the two are never merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent oidc_refresh calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9 single-flight guard the cookie-session refresh() uses, so an oidc_refresh and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never interleave.

def device_login( self, on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None], *, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
1878    def device_login(
1879        self,
1880        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None],
1881        *,
1882        scope: str | None = None,
1883        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1884        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1885    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1886        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
1887        user code, poll to completion.
1888
1889        ``on_user_code`` is called with the :class:`DeviceAuthorization`
1890        **before the first poll** — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have
1891        had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK
1892        never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink
1893        panel) is the application's decision.
1894
1895        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
1896        set rather than adopting it, matching its ``login_client_credentials``
1897        posture.
1898
1899        Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response;
1900        ``slow_down`` adds 5 s **permanently**; ``authorization_pending``
1901        loops; ``access_denied`` and ``expired_token`` raise distinct errors;
1902        polling stops at ``expires_in`` even if the server has not yet said
1903        ``expired_token``. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is **not**
1904        terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by
1905        the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the
1906        user has already approved.
1907        """
1908        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1909        authorization = self.device_authorize(
1910            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
1911        )
1912
1913        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
1914        on_user_code(authorization)
1915
1916        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
1917        while True:
1918            if not schedule.tick():
1919                raise self._device_expired_error()
1920            time.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
1921            try:
1922                return self.device_poll(
1923                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
1924                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
1925                    configuration=config,
1926                )
1927            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
1928                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
1929                if outcome == "pending" or outcome == "retry":
1930                    continue
1931                if outcome == "slow_down":
1932                    schedule.slow_down()
1933                    continue
1934                raise

The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the user code, poll to completion.

on_user_code is called with the DeviceAuthorization before the first poll — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink panel) is the application's decision.

Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK returns the token set rather than adopting it, matching its login_client_credentials posture.

Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response; slow_down adds 5 s permanently; authorization_pending loops; access_denied and expired_token raise distinct errors; polling stops at expires_in even if the server has not yet said expired_token. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is not terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the user has already approved.

def token_exchange( self, *, subject_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, subject_token_type: str, actor_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str | None = None, scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None, audience: str | None = None, resource: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> ExchangedToken: 
1936    def token_exchange(
1937        self,
1938        *,
1939        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
1940        subject_token_type: str,
1941        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
1942        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
1943        audience: str | None = None,
1944        resource: str | None = None,
1945        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1946        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1947    ) -> ExchangedToken:
1948        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (CONTRACT.md §15.1)
1949        — exchange a token for a **narrower** one.
1950
1951        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1952
1953        * **No default ``actor_token``** (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for
1954          *impersonation*; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own
1955          session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
1956        * **No retry or downgrade on ``unauthorized_client``** (rule 2) — a
1957          registration fact an operator must fix.
1958        * **No auto-narrowing on ``invalid_scope``** (rule 3). The server
1959          refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds
1960          out here.
1961        * **No adoption** (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one
1962          outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every
1963          subsequent call this client makes.
1964
1965        A cross-tenant subject token answers ``invalid_grant``, identically to
1966        an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the
1967        server collapses them because distinguishing them is a
1968        tenant-enumeration signal.
1969
1970        Args:
1971            subject_token_type: What kind of token ``subject_token`` is.
1972                ``None`` sends :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE`, the
1973                same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a
1974                **trusted external issuer** (§15.7), set this explicitly —
1975                normally to :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE`. The SDK
1976                never reads ``subject_token`` to decide the value: which kind
1977                of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses
1978                refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry
1979                a refusal as a different type.
1980
1981        Raises:
1982            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1983                with no wire call.
1984        """
1985        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1986        form = self._token_exchange_form(
1987            subject_token=subject_token,
1988            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
1989            actor_token=actor_token,
1990            scopes=scopes,
1991            audience=audience,
1992            resource=resource,
1993        )
1994        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1995        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1996        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
1997        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)

POST /oauth2/token with the RFC 8693 grant (CONTRACT.md §15.1) — exchange a token for a narrower one.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default actor_token (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for impersonation; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
  • No retry or downgrade on unauthorized_client (rule 2) — a registration fact an operator must fix.
  • No auto-narrowing on invalid_scope (rule 3). The server refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds out here.
  • No adoption (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every subsequent call this client makes.

A cross-tenant subject token answers invalid_grant, identically to an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the server collapses them because distinguishing them is a tenant-enumeration signal.

Args: subject_token_type: What kind of token subject_token is. None sends ~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE, the same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a trusted external issuer (§15.7), set this explicitly — normally to ~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE. The SDK never reads subject_token to decide the value: which kind of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry a refusal as a different type.

Raises: AuthError: when no client_secret was configured — client-side, with no wire call.

2073    def uma_request_ticket(

2081        server draws rather than flattening it.

2088            "POST",

2095            "dict[str, str]",

2097        )

def uma_exchange_ticket( self, *, ticket: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, claim_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> RequestingPartyToken: 
2100    def uma_exchange_ticket(
2101        self,
2102        *,
2103        ticket: SecretStr | str,
2104        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
2105        tenant_id: str | None = None,
2106        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
2107    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
2108        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange
2109        a ticket for an RPT.
2110
2111        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
2112        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
2113        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
2114        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
2115        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the
2116        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
2117        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a
2118        **new** ticket.
2119
2120        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
2121
2122        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
2123          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
2124          resource server instead of for the user.
2125        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
2126          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
2127          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
2128        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
2129          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
2130          that user.
2131
2132        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
2133        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
2134        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
2135        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
2136
2137        Raises:
2138            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
2139                with no wire call.
2140        """
2141        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
2142        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
2143        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
2144        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
2145        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2146        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)

POST /oauth2/token with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a ticket for an RPT.

This method never retries. It issues exactly one request and is outside the §16 retry policy — not on 5xx, not on timeout, not on any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed before the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a new ticket.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default claim_token (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the resource server instead of for the user.
  • No auto-narrowing on access_denied (rule 3). A partial grant is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the application's judgement, not this SDK's.
  • No adoption (rule 4). The RPT is the requesting party's token. Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as that user.

The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client — all answer invalid_grant with one message. This SDK does not try to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller cannot probe for live ticket handles.

Raises: AuthError: when no client_secret was configured — client-side, with no wire call.

def logout_url( self, *, id_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, post_logout_redirect_uri: str | None = None, state: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> str: 
2148    def logout_url(
2149        self,
2150        *,
2151        id_token: SecretStr | str,
2152        post_logout_redirect_uri: str | None = None,
2153        state: str | None = None,
2154        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
2155    ) -> str:
2156        """Build the RP-initiated logout URL to redirect the user agent to
2157        (CONTRACT.md §12.7.2).
2158

2160        anyway, and does **not** clear this client's own session: whether the
2161        local session ends is the application's decision — a backend holding a
2162        service-account session must not lose it because a *user* logged out.
2163
2164        ``end_session_endpoint`` is read from discovery and never synthesised
2165        from the issuer (rule 1). ``post_logout_redirect_uri`` is passed
2166        through unvalidated against any local list (rule 3): the allow-list
2167        lives in the client's server-side registration, and a client-side copy
2168        would drift and reject a URI an operator had just registered.
2169
2170        ``state`` is the caller's to generate and the caller's to check; the
2171        SDK never invents one, because the value only means something to the
2172        application that will receive it back.
2173        """
2174        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
2175        return self._logout_url_impl(
2176            config,
2177            id_token=id_token,
2178            post_logout_redirect_uri=post_logout_redirect_uri,
2179            state=state,
2180        )

Build the RP-initiated logout URL to redirect the user agent to (CONTRACT.md §12.7.2).

Performs no network I/O beyond the discovery fetch the SDK caches anyway, and does not clear this client's own session: whether the local session ends is the application's decision — a backend holding a service-account session must not lose it because a user logged out.

end_session_endpoint is read from discovery and never synthesised from the issuer (rule 1). post_logout_redirect_uri is passed through unvalidated against any local list (rule 3): the allow-list lives in the client's server-side registration, and a client-side copy would drift and reject a URI an operator had just registered.

state is the caller's to generate and the caller's to check; the SDK never invents one, because the value only means something to the application that will receive it back.

def verify_logout_token( self, token: str, *, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> VerifiedLogoutToken: 
2182    def verify_logout_token(
2183        self,
2184        token: str,
2185        *,
2186        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
2187    ) -> VerifiedLogoutToken:
2188        """Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this
2189        application's ``backchannel_logout_uri`` (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).
2190
2191        Every check exists because skipping it has a name:
2192
2193        1. **Signature**, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token
2194           path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same
2195           ``kid``-required discipline.
2196        2. **``iss``/``aud``**: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
2197        3. **``events`` carries the back-channel-logout key.** This is what
2198           distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means
2199           accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
2200        4. **``nonce`` is absent.** Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it,
2201           and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being
2202           replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
2203        5. **At least one of ``sid``/``sub``** — a token naming neither
2204           identifies nothing.
2205        6. **``exp`` in the future, ``iat`` recent.**
2206
2207        Returns:
2208            The ``sid``/``sub``/``jti`` the token names — never a bare
2209            ``bool``, because the RP has to know *which* session to end.
2210            **Dedup on ``jti`` yourself**: delivery is at-least-once, so a
2211            valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard
2212            would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second
2213            logout after a restart.
2214        """
2215        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
2216        return self._verify_logout_token_impl(token, config)

Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this application's backchannel_logout_uri (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).

Every check exists because skipping it has a name:

  1. Signature, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same kid-required discipline.
  2. iss/aud: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
  3. events carries the back-channel-logout key. This is what distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
  4. nonce is absent. Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it, and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
  5. At least one of sid/sub — a token naming neither identifies nothing.
  6. exp in the future, iat recent.

Returns: The sid/sub/jti the token names — never a bare bool, because the RP has to know which session to end. Dedup on jti yourself: delivery is at-least-once, so a valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second logout after a restart.

2338        redirect_uri: str,

2340        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
2341        org_id: str | None = None,
2342        org_slug: str | None = None,

2344        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/start`` (CONTRACT.md
2345        §12.1) — step 1 of a login through a **plain-OAuth2** upstream
2346        (GitHub, Facebook, ``generic_oauth2``).
2347
2348        Call this, rather than :meth:`sso_start`, exactly when the
2349        provider's ``protocol`` is ``OAuth2`` (§12.1 note 10). The server
2350        refuses a mismatch with ``400`` rather than accepting it silently,
2351        so a client that assumes OIDC fails on every GitHub button.
2352
2353        PKCE is mandatory on this path and is generated and stored
2354        **server-side**; nothing about it appears in the request or the
2355        response (§12.1 note 11).
2356
2357        A ``400`` here can mean the ``redirect_uri`` is not on an origin the
2358        deployment accepts (§12.1 rule 12a); it surfaces as
2359        :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` and is not retried.
2360        """
2361        body = self._sso_start_oauth2_body(
2362            federation_config_id=federation_config_id,

POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/start (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — step 1 of a login through a plain-OAuth2 upstream (GitHub, Facebook, generic_oauth2).

Call this, rather than sso_start(), exactly when the provider's protocol is OAuth2 (§12.1 note 10). The server refuses a mismatch with 400 rather than accepting it silently, so a client that assumes OIDC fails on every GitHub button.

PKCE is mandatory on this path and is generated and stored server-side; nothing about it appears in the request or the response (§12.1 note 11).

A 400 here can mean the redirect_uri is not on an origin the deployment accepts (§12.1 rule 12a); it surfaces as ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError and is not retried.
