def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult: 
2393    def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
2394        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/handoff`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
2395        redeem the single-use code the SAML and Apple flows deliver.
2396
2397        Those two protocols return **cross-site**, so the server cannot set
2398        ``SameSite=Strict`` session cookies on that response. It instead
2399        redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an
2400        ``axiam_handoff`` query parameter (``HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM``); this
2401        call posts that code back same-origin, and *this* response is the
2402        one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).
2403
2404        **The code is gone either way.** It is valid for
2405        ``HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`` seconds and redeemable **once**. Redeem
2406        it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed
2407        redemption: a ``401`` is terminal, and this method makes exactly one
2408        wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown,
2409        expired and already-redeemed all answer the same ``401``,
2410        deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to
2411        do.
2412        """
2413        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2414            "POST", SSO_HANDOFF_PATH, json={"code": code}
2415        )
2416        response = self._rest_send_sync(request)
2417        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteHandoff")

Those two protocols return cross-site, so the server cannot set SameSite=Strict session cookies on that response. It instead redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an axiam_handoff query parameter (HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM); this call posts that code back same-origin, and this response is the one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).

The code is gone either way. It is valid for HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS seconds and redeemable once. Redeem it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed redemption: a 401 is terminal, and this method makes exactly one wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown, expired and already-redeemed all answer the same 401, deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to do.

2579    def webauthn_setup_register_finish(
2580        self,
2581        *,
2582        setup_token: SecretStr | str,
2583        state_token: SecretStr | str,
2584        credential_name: str,
2585        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
2586    ) -> LoginResult:
2587        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/setup/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md
2588        §24.1, §25.2 rule 2 — contract 1.45).
2589
2590        Completes the login ``login()`` interrupted, exactly as
2591        :meth:`mfa_setup_confirm` does for TOTP: adopts credentials on success
2592        (§24.3's five rules apply verbatim, per §25.2 rule 2) and clears the
2593        §17 decision memo because the subject changed. Takes no session, for
2594        the same reason :meth:`webauthn_setup_register_start` does not — a
2595        second credential on a call whose only credential is meant to be the
2596        setup token invites a server that changes its mind about which to
2597        trust.
2598
2599        A ``403`` here is the tenant's attestation policy refusing **this
2600        authenticator** — an AAGUID that is not allow-listed, a missing FIDO
2601        certification, a revoked status — and its message is surfaced
2602        verbatim (§24.4 rule 1): it is the only way the person holding the
2603        key learns that a different one would work.
2604        """
2605        self._ensure_open()
2606        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
2607        # this call changes the subject.
2608        self._on_credential_change()
2609        body = self._webauthn_setup_register_finish_body(
2610            setup_token, state_token, credential_name, response
2611        )
2612        request = self._session._credential_free_request(
2613            "POST", self._WA_SETUP_REGISTER_FINISH, body
2614        )
2615        http_response = self._session._send_sync_credential_free(request)
2616        return self._handle_setup_register_finish_response(http_response)

Completes the login login() interrupted, exactly as mfa_setup_confirm() does for TOTP: adopts credentials on success (§24.3's five rules apply verbatim, per §25.2 rule 2) and clears the §17 decision memo because the subject changed. Takes no session, for the same reason webauthn_setup_register_start() does not — a second credential on a call whose only credential is meant to be the setup token invites a server that changes its mind about which to trust.

A 403 here is the tenant's attestation policy refusing this authenticator — an AAGUID that is not allow-listed, a missing FIDO certification, a revoked status — and its message is surfaced verbatim (§24.4 rule 1): it is the only way the person holding the key learns that a different one would work.

2710    def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
2711        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
2712        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
2713        and say what happened.
2714
2715        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
2716        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
2717        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
2718        address.
2719
2720        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
2721        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
2722        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
2723
2724        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
2725          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
2726          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
2727          succeeding.
2728        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
2729          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
2730        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
2731
2732        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
2733        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
2734        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
2735        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
2736        """
2737        self._ensure_open()
2738        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
2739            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
2740        )
2741        self._expect_no_content(self._rest_send_sync(request), "resend_own_verification")

POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification (CONTRACT.md §25.1, §25.7) — resend the signed-in caller's own verification mail, and say what happened.

Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary address.

Unlike resend_verification() this reports the outcome, because the caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:

  • returns — a token was minted and the mail enqueued. Delivery is asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this succeeding.
  • ~axiam_sdk.ConflictError (from 409) — already verified, or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
  • ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError (from 429) — the daily limit.

§25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.

class AsyncAxiamClient(axiam_sdk._client._AxiamClientBase, axiam_sdk.management.ops.AsyncManagementNamespaces): 
  89class AsyncAxiamClient(_AxiamClientBase, AsyncManagementNamespaces):
  90    """The AXIAM SDK's dedicated async REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10,
  91    SDK-Q08).
  92
  93    ``await client.login(...)`` returns a typed
  94    :class:`~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult` with ``mfa_required`` (SC#1) — the
  95    same contract as the sync :class:`~axiam_sdk.AxiamClient`, on its own
  96    dedicated async object. Constructing both an ``AxiamClient`` and an
  97    ``AsyncAxiamClient`` against the same ``base_url``/``tenant_slug`` gives
  98    each its own independent ``_Session`` (cookie jar, CSRF state, refresh
  99    guard) — the two classes do NOT share session state with each other, only
 100    each shares consistently within its own sync or async call path.
 101    """
 102
 103    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 104    # Lifecycle (D-19)
 105    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 106
 107    async def __aenter__(self) -> AsyncAxiamClient:
 108        """Async context-manager entry — returns ``self`` (D-19); no
 109        separate setup beyond what ``__init__`` already did."""
 110        return self
 111
 112    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
 113        """Async context-manager exit — always calls :meth:`aclose`,
 114        regardless of whether the ``async with`` block raised (D-19)."""
 115        await self.aclose()
 116
 117    async def aclose(self) -> None:
 118        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
 119
 120        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
 121        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
 122
 123        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
 124        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
 125        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
 126        restart and resume; an ``aclose()`` that logged out would silently end
 127        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
 128        ending the session is what you want.
 129
 130        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
 131        rather than silently reconnecting.
 132        """
 133        self._closed = True
 134        self._decision_memo.clear()
 135        await self._session.aclose()
 136
 137    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 138    # acting tenant (CONTRACT.md §5.2 rule 1, contract 1.51)
 139    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 140
 141    def acting_tenant(self, tenant_id: str) -> AsyncAxiamClient:
 142        """A handle to this client that acts on ``tenant_id`` — CONTRACT.md
 143        §5.2 rule 1 (contract 1.51).
 144
 145        Synchronous — it performs no I/O, only a client-side gate — and
 146        otherwise identical to :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.acting_tenant`:
 147        the returned handle shares session, cookie jar, refresh guard,
 148        telemetry and decision memo with ``self``, and differs only in the
 149        ``X-Axiam-Tenant`` it sends. See that method's docstring for the
 150        gating rules and what the header does and does not reach.
 151
 152        Raises:
 153            NetworkError: if ``tenant_id`` is not a UUID.
 154            AuthzError: per :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.acting_tenant`.
 155        """
 156        normalized = self._check_acting_tenant_gate(tenant_id)
 157        handle = copy.copy(self)
 158        handle._acting_tenant = normalized
 159        return handle
 160
 161    def clear_acting_tenant(self) -> AsyncAxiamClient:
 162        """A handle to this client that sends **no** ``X-Axiam-Tenant``. See
 163        :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.clear_acting_tenant`."""
 164        handle = copy.copy(self)
 165        handle._acting_tenant = None
 166        return handle
 167
 168    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 169    # mTLS device login (CONTRACT.md §6.1 rules 6-10, contract 1.51)
 170    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 171
 172    async def authenticate_device(self) -> DeviceToken:
 173        """``POST /api/v1/auth/device`` (CONTRACT.md §6.1) — the mTLS device
 174        login. See :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.authenticate_device` for the
 175        full contract; this is its async twin."""
 176        self._ensure_open()
 177        self._reachable_only_with_client_cert("authenticate_device")
 178        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", DEVICE_AUTH_PATH)
 179        # See AxiamClient.authenticate_device: this call mints the bearer
 180        # credential, so it must withhold the jar itself rather than rely
 181        # on _apply_bearer_credential, which only fires once one is held.
 182        request.headers["Cookie"] = ""
 183        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 184        return self._handle_device_auth_response(response)
 185
 186    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 187    # login / verify_mfa
 188    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 189
 190    async def login(self, email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 191        """``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` (CONTRACT.md §1). Returns a typed
 192        :class:`LoginResult`; check ``mfa_required`` before assuming the
 193        session is established (SC#1)."""
 194        self._ensure_open()
 195        self._on_credential_change()
 196        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 197            "POST", LOGIN_PATH, json=self._login_body(email, password)
 198        )
 199        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 200        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 201
 202    async def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 203        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
 204
 205        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.login_opaque`; see that method for
 206        the full contract — including what the ``login/start`` response's
 207        ``mode`` field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under
 208        ``"optional"`` this retries over :meth:`login` and returns that call's
 209        outcome, and under ``"required"``, an unrecognised value or no ``mode``
 210        at all it raises :class:`AuthError` and retries nothing. Returns the
 211        same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
 212        ``mfa_required`` case.
 213
 214        The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it:
 215        Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a
 216        server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in
 217        :func:`asyncio.to_thread`.
 218        """
 219        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
 220
 221        self._ensure_open()
 222        self._on_credential_change()
 223
 224        exchange = start_login(password)
 225
 226        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 227            "POST",
 228            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
 229            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
 230        )
 231        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 232        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 233            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
 234        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
 235
 236        try:
 237            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
 238        except AuthError:
 239            # §23.4 rule 7, decided identically to the sync client — the shared
 240            # `allows_password_fallback` is what keeps the two from drifting.
 241            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
 242                raise
 243            return await self.login(username_or_email, password)
 244
 245        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 246            "POST",
 247            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
 248            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
 249        )
 250        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 251        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
 252            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
 253        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 254
 255    async def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 256        """Build a registration record for *password*, sealed against the tenant
 257        this client is **acting on**.
 258
 259        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.opaque_enrollment`; see that method
 260        for the full contract, including why the caller's *own* password change
 261        wants :meth:`opaque_enrollment_for_self` instead.
 262        """
 263        return await self._enroll(password, None)
 264
 265    async def opaque_enrollment_for_self(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 266        """Build a registration record for the **caller's own** new password,
 267        sealed against the tenant the caller's account lives in.
 268
 269        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.opaque_enrollment_for_self`; see
 270        that method for the full contract (CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 2).
 271        """
 272        if self._principal_tenant_id is None:
 273            raise NetworkError(
 274                "OPAQUE: no principal tenant is known yet — sign in before "
 275                "building a registration record for your own password"
 276            )
 277        return await self._enroll(password, self._principal_tenant_id)
 278
 279    async def _enroll(self, password: str, principal_tenant_id: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
 280        """The shared body of the two enrolment methods; they differ only in the
 281        tenant the record is sealed against."""
 282        from ._opaque import KsfParams, start_registration
 283
 284        self._ensure_open()
 285        exchange = start_registration(password)
 286
 287        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 288            "POST",
 289            OPAQUE_REGISTER_START_PATH,
 290            json=self._opaque_register_start_body(exchange.request, principal_tenant_id),
 291        )
 292        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 293        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 294            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "register/start")
 295        started = response.json()
 296
 297        return {
 298            "opaque_session": started["opaque_session"],
 299            "registration_record": exchange.finish(
 300                password, started["registration_response"], KsfParams.from_wire(started)
 301            ),
 302        }
 303
 304    async def verify_mfa(self, mfa_token: Any, code: str) -> LoginResult:
 305        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — completes the
 306        two-phase flow started by :meth:`login` when ``mfa_required`` was
 307        true."""
 308        self._ensure_open()
 309        self._on_credential_change()
 310        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 311            "POST", MFA_VERIFY_PATH, json=self._mfa_verify_body(mfa_token, code)
 312        )
 313        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 314        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 315
 316    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 317    # refresh — exactly one literal /api/v1/auth/refresh POST, routed
 318    # through the single-flight guard (Pitfall 4, §9.3)
 319    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 320
 321    async def refresh(self) -> None:
 322        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
 323        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
 324        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
 325        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
 326        self._ensure_open()
 327        self._on_credential_change()
 328        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
 329        if not observed_access:
 330            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
 331
 332        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
 333        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
 334        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
 335        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
 336        await self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_async(
 337            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_async(tenant_id, org_id)
 338        )
 339
 340    async def _do_refresh_async(self, tenant_id: str, org_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 341        """Perform the actual ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` call — the
 342        ``do_refresh`` closure passed to
 343        :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.refresh_if_needed_async`
 344        by :meth:`refresh`. Not called directly by SDK users; always routed
 345        through the single-flight guard so concurrent 401s collapse into
 346        one in-flight call (§9)."""
 347        # The literal /api/v1/auth/refresh path is required so the
 348        # Path-scoped axiam_refresh cookie attaches (Pitfall 4).
 349        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 350            "POST", "/api/v1/auth/refresh", json=self._refresh_body(tenant_id, org_id)
 351        )
 352        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 353        return self._handle_refresh_response(response)
 354
 355    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 356    # logout
 357    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 358
 359    async def logout(self) -> None:
 360        """``POST /api/v1/auth/logout`` (CONTRACT.md §1)."""
 361        self._ensure_open()
 362        self._on_credential_change()
 363        session_id = self._session_id_for_logout()
 364        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 365            "POST", LOGOUT_PATH, json={"session_id": session_id}
 366        )
 367        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 368        if response.status_code >= 300:
 369            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "logout failed", response=response)
 370        self._session.refresh_guard = type(self._session.refresh_guard)()
 371        # CONTRACT.md §6.1 rule 4 / CONTRACT 1.52 N4.4: logout clears a
 372        # held device credential, same as it clears the cookie session.
 373        self._session.clear_bearer_credential()
 374        # §5.2 rule 1: no session, no reach to gate `acting_tenant()` on.
 375        self._principal_scope = None
 376
 377    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 378    # REST authz: check_access / can / batch_check
 379    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 380
 381    async def check_access(
 382        self,
 383        action: str,
 384        resource_id: str,
 385        scope: str | None = None,
 386        *,
 387        subject_id: str | None = None,
 388    ) -> AccessResult:
 389        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
 390
 391        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
 392        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
 393        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
 394        declarative ``require_access`` helper (§11) passes to check the
 395        *request's* authenticated user rather than this client's own
 396        (often service-account) session.
 397        """
 398        self._ensure_open()
 399        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
 400        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
 401        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id, self._acting_tenant)
 402        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
 403        if memoized is not None:
 404            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
 405            return memoized
 406
 407        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
 408        wire = await self._authz_post_async(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
 409        result = AccessResult(**wire)
 410
 411        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
 412        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
 413        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
 414        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
 415        return result
 416
 417    async def can(self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None) -> bool:
 418        """Alias for ``check_access`` returning only the allowed boolean
 419        (CONTRACT.md §1 note, browser/UI scenarios)."""
 420        result = await self.check_access(action, resource_id, scope)
 421        return result.allowed
 422
 423    async def batch_check(self, checks: list[AccessCheck]) -> list[AccessResult]:
 424        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check/batch`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — results
 425        returned in the same order as ``checks``."""
 426        body = {"checks": [c.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for c in checks]}
 427        wire = await self._authz_post_async(BATCH_CHECK_PATH, body, operation="batch_check")
 428        return BatchCheckResult(**wire).results
 429
 430    async def _authz_post_async(
 431        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], *, operation: str
 432    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 433        """POST an authz request body to *path* under the §16 retry policy.
 434
 435        The call is a ``POST`` but changes no server state, so it is
 436        retry-eligible: §16.2's test is "changes no server state", NOT "is a
 437        GET". Gating on the verb would exclude the single most important
 438        operation this policy covers.
 439
 440        The §9.3 refresh-then-retry-once on a 401 is a *different* mechanism and
 441        stays inside one §16 attempt: a 401 means the token expired, which
 442        refreshing fixes, and neither backing off nor counting it against the
 443        transport-failure budget would make sense.
 444        """
 445        return await retry_async(
 446            lambda attempt: self._authz_post_async_once(path, body, operation, attempt),
 447            operation=operation,
 448            enabled=self._retry_enabled,
 449            telemetry=self._telemetry,
 450        )
 451
 452    async def _authz_post_async_once(
 453        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], operation: str, attempt: int
 454    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 455        """One §16 attempt, with its §19 request pair."""
 456        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
 457        with self._telemetry.request(operation, "POST", path, attempt) as span:
 458            response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 459
 460            # CONTRACT.md §6.1 rule 5 / CONTRACT 1.52 N4.5: a device
 461            # credential is never refreshed, on either transport. Leaving
 462            # `response` as the server's own 401 when one is held means the
 463            # status check below raises with the SERVER's message, never
 464            # the refresh guard's "no access token to refresh".
 465            if (
 466                response.status_code == httpx.codes.UNAUTHORIZED
 467                and self._session.bearer_token is None
 468            ):
 469                response = await self._retry_after_refresh_async(request)
 470
 471            span.status = response.status_code
 472            if response.status_code < 200 or response.status_code >= 300:
 473                raise error_from_http_status(
 474                    response.status_code, "authz check failed", response=response
 475                )
 476            span.outcome = "success"
 477            result: dict[str, Any] = response.json()
 478            return result
 479
 480    async def _retry_after_refresh_async(self, original_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
 481        """On a 401, refresh exactly once (via the shared single-flight
 482        guard) then retry the failed authz call exactly once. A second
 483        failure propagates through the caller's own status check (§9.3, no
 484        retry loop)."""
 485        await self.refresh()
 486        retry_request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 487            original_request.method,
 488            original_request.url,
 489            content=original_request.content,
 490            headers={
 491                k: v
 492                for k, v in original_request.headers.items()
 493                if k.lower() not in ("content-length", "x-csrf-token")
 494            },
 495        )
 496        return await self._rest_send_async(retry_request)
 497
 498    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 499    # OIDC / SSO relying-party helpers (CONTRACT.md §12, Task T3, SDK-Q08)
 500    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 501
 502    async def oidc_discover(self) -> OidcConfiguration:
 503        """``GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
 504        fetch the OIDC discovery document, cached per origin with a
 505        ≥5-minute TTL and single-flight de-duplication of concurrent calls
 506        (§12.3 rule 6)."""
 507
 508        async def fetch() -> OidcConfiguration:
 509            """Perform the actual discovery-document GET; called by the
 510            discovery cache at most once per cache miss/expiry."""
 511            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("GET", DISCOVERY_PATH)
 512            response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 513            return self._parse_discovery_response(response)
 514
 515        return await self._discovery_cache.get_async(self._discovery_origin_key(), fetch)
 516
 517    async def oidc_begin(
 518        self,
 519        *,
 520        configuration: OidcConfiguration,
 521        redirect_uri: str,
 522        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
 523        extra_params: dict[str, str] | None = None,
 524    ) -> AuthorizationRequest:
 525        """Build an authorization request (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — **pure
 526        local computation, no network I/O**; this ``async def`` has no
 527        internal ``await`` (CONTRACT.md §12.2's Python naming table gives
 528        ``oidc_begin`` no synchronous carve-out the way it does for C#).
 529        Nothing is stored: persist the returned ``state``, ``nonce``, and
 530        ``code_verifier`` yourself (§12.3 rule 1)."""
 531        return self._oidc_begin_impl(
 532            configuration=configuration,
 533            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
 534            scope=scope,
 535            extra_params=extra_params,
 536        )
 537
 538    async def oidc_par(
 539        self,
 540        *,
 541        request: AuthorizationRequest,
 542        redirect_uri: str,
 543        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
 544        dpop_jkt: str | None = None,
 545        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 546        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 547    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
 548        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
 549        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
 550        with.
 551
 552        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
 553        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
 554        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
 555        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
 556        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
 557        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
 558
 559        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
 560        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
 561        authorize any other way (§21.1).
 562
 563        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
 564        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
 565
 566        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
 567        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
 568        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
 569        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
 570
 571        ``dpop_jkt`` (RFC 9449 §10.1) binds the authorization code this push
 572        will produce to a DPoP key before the browser ever sees a redirect, so
 573        the code cannot be exchanged by whoever intercepts it. Pass the RFC
 574        7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key the token request will prove
 575        possession of; :func:`axiam_sdk._dpop.jwk_thumbprint_s256` computes it
 576        from a JWK. It is caller-supplied rather than derived because this SDK
 577        holds no DPoP key of its own (§21.9): it verifies proofs, it does not
 578        mint them. Omitted from the form entirely when ``None``.
 579
 580        Raises:
 581            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
 582                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
 583            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
 584        """
 585        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 586        form = self._par_form(
 587            request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope, dpop_jkt=dpop_jkt
 588        )
 589        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
 590        http_request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 591        response = await self._rest_send_async(http_request)
 592        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)
 593
 594    async def oidc_exchange(
 595        self,
 596        *,
 597        code: str,
 598        code_verifier: SecretStr | str,
 599        redirect_uri: str,
 600        nonce: str,
 601        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 602        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 603    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 604        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=authorization_code``
 605        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — exchange an authorization code for a token
 606        set, validating the returned ID token in full before returning
 607        (§12.4). On ANY §12.4 failure the whole token set is discarded and
 608        ``AuthError`` is raised with the matching reason code (§12.4
 609        rule 7) — the access/refresh token from the same response is never
 610        returned."""
 611        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 612        form = self._exchange_form(
 613            code=code, code_verifier=code_verifier, redirect_uri=redirect_uri
 614        )
 615        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 616        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 617        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 618        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, nonce)
 619
 620    async def oidc_refresh(
 621        self,
 622        *,
 623        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
 624        scope: str | None = None,
 625        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 626        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 627    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 628        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
 629        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
 630
 631        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
 632        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
 633        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
 634        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
 635        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
 636        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
 637        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
 638        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
 639        interleave.
 640        """
 641
 642        async def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
 643            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
 644            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_async`
 645            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
 646            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
 647            config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 648            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
 649            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 650            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 651            response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 652            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
 653            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 654
 655        async def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
 656            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
 657            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
 658            :meth:`refresh` call."""
 659            token_set: OidcTokenSet = await self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_async(
 660                do_refresh
 661            )
 662            return token_set
 663
 664        result: OidcTokenSet = await self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_async.run(under_guard)
 665        return result
 666
 667    async def login_client_credentials(
 668        self,
 669        *,
 670        scope: str | None = None,
 671        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 672        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 673    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 674        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=client_credentials``
 675        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — service-account machine-to-machine login.
 676        Requests no ``openid`` scope, so the response carries no
 677        ``id_token``.
 678
 679        Raises:
 680            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — this
 681                grant cannot be performed by a public client.
 682        """
 683        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 684        form = self._client_credentials_form(scope=scope)
 685        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 686        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 687        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 688        # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to this grant.
 689        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 690
 691    async def device_authorize(
 692        self,
 693        *,
 694        scope: str | None = None,
 695        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 696        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 697    ) -> DeviceAuthorization:
 698        """``POST /oauth2/device_authorization`` (CONTRACT.md §14.1) — start
 699        the device grant and obtain the code pair.
 700
 701        **Unauthenticated by design**: a device that cannot show a browser also
 702        cannot hold a client secret, so this never sends ``client_secret`` and
 703        never refuses a client built without one.
 704
 705        Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.device_authorize`; §14.4
 706        requires the same three names on both clients.
 707        """
 708        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 709        form = self._device_authorize_form(scope=scope)
 710        url = self._device_authorization_url(config, tenant_id)
 711        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 712        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 713        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 714            raise error_from_oauth2_response(
 715                response.status_code, response, "device authorization request failed"
 716            )
 717        return self._build_device_authorization(response.json())
 718
 719    async def device_poll(
 720        self,
 721        *,
 722        device_code: SecretStr | str,
 723        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 724        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 725    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 726        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the device-code grant (§14.1) — **one**
 727        poll attempt.
 728
 729        The five RFC 8628 §3.5 answers surface as ``OAuthProtocolError``,
 730        ``authorization_pending`` and ``slow_down`` included, so a hand-rolled
 731        loop sees exactly what :meth:`device_login` sees.
 732        """
 733        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 734        form = self._device_poll_form(device_code=device_code)
 735        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 736        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 737        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 738        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 739
 740    async def device_login(
 741        self,
 742        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]],
 743        *,
 744        scope: str | None = None,
 745        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 746        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 747    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 748        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
 749        user code, poll to completion.
 750
 751        ``on_user_code`` is invoked — and **awaited when it returns an
 752        awaitable** — before the first poll (§14.3 rule 2). A device rendering
 753        a QR code may need to await a paint, and polling before that resolves
 754        would defeat the rule as surely as not calling back at all.
 755
 756        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
 757        set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync
 758        twin's docstring for the full rule set.
 759        """
 760        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 761        authorization = await self.device_authorize(
 762            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
 763        )
 764
 765        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
 766        result = on_user_code(authorization)
 767        if isinstance(result, Awaitable):
 768            await result
 769
 770        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
 771        while True:
 772            if not schedule.tick():
 773                raise self._device_expired_error()
 774            await asyncio.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
 775            try:
 776                return await self.device_poll(
 777                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
 778                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
 779                    configuration=config,
 780                )
 781            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
 782                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
 783                if outcome in ("pending", "retry"):
 784                    continue
 785                if outcome == "slow_down":
 786                    schedule.slow_down()
 787                    continue
 788                raise
 789
 790    async def token_exchange(
 791        self,
 792        *,
 793        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
 794        subject_token_type: str,
 795        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
 796        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
 797        audience: str | None = None,
 798        resource: str | None = None,
 799        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 800        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 801    ) -> ExchangedToken:
 802        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (§15.1) — exchange a
 803        token for a **narrower** one.
 804
 805        Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.token_exchange`; see that
 806        docstring for what this method deliberately refuses to do (no
 807        defaulted ``actor_token``, no auto-narrowing, no adoption) and for
 808        ``subject_token_type``, which reaches the external exchange of §15.7
 809        and is never inferred from the token.
 810        """
 811        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 812        form = self._token_exchange_form(
 813            subject_token=subject_token,
 814            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
 815            actor_token=actor_token,
 816            scopes=scopes,
 817            audience=audience,
 818            resource=resource,
 819        )
 820        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 821        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 822        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 823        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)
 824
 825    async def uma_register_resource(
 826        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource: ResourceSet

 828        """``POST /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — register a resource set
 829        (CONTRACT.md §20.1).

 839        )
 840        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 841        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource registration failed")

 844    async def uma_read_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str) -> ResourceSet:
 845        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — read a resource set (§20.1)."""

 855    async def uma_update_resource(
 856        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str, resource: ResourceSet
 857    ) -> ResourceSet:
 858        """``PUT /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — replace a resource set (§20.1).
 859
 860        **The scope list is replaced, not merged** (§20.2 rule 8). Whatever
 861        ``resource.resource_scopes`` holds becomes the complete declared set;
 862        omitting a scope removes it, which is how a resource server drops an
 863        authority. This method performs no read-before-write.
 864        """
 865        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 866            "PUT",
 867            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
 868            json=self._uma_resource_payload(resource),
 869            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
 870        )
 871        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 872        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource update failed")
 873        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

 876        """``DELETE /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — deregister (§20.1)."""

 880            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
 881        )

 883        self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource delete failed")

 885    async def uma_list_resources(self, pat: SecretStr | str) -> list[str]:
 886        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — list the ids **this client**
 887        registered (§20.1).
 888
 889        Not the tenant's whole resource tree: a protection scope does not
 890        entitle a caller to enumerate it.
 891        """
 892        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(

 901    async def uma_request_ticket(
 902        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
 903    ) -> SecretStr:
 904        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
 905
 906        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
 907        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
 908        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
 909        server draws rather than flattening it.
 910        """
 911        body = [
 912            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
 913            for p in permissions
 914        ]
 915        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 916            "POST",
 917            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
 918            json=body,
 919            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
 920        )
 921        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 922        wire = cast(
 923            "dict[str, str]",
 924            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
 925        )
 926        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])
 927
 928    async def uma_exchange_ticket(
 929        self,
 930        *,
 931        ticket: SecretStr | str,
 932        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
 933        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 934        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 935    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
 936        """Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.uma_exchange_ticket`.
 937
 938        ``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a
 939        ticket for an RPT.
 940
 941        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
 942        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
 943        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
 944        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
 945        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second
 946        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
 947        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On
 948        failure, request a **new** ticket.
 949
 950        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
 951
 952        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
 953          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
 954          resource server instead of for the user.
 955        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
 956          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
 957          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
 958        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
 959          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
 960          that user.
 961
 962        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
 963        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
 964        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
 965        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
 966
 967        Raises:
 968            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
 969                with no wire call.
 970        """
 971        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 972        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
 973        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 974        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 975        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
 976        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)
 977

1014    async def introspect(
1015        self,
1016        *,
1017        token: SecretStr | str,
1018        token_type_hint: str | None = None,
1019        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1020        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1021    ) -> IntrospectionResult:
1022        """``POST /oauth2/introspect`` (RFC 7662, CONTRACT.md §12.1) — ask
1023        the server whether a token is active and, if so, for its metadata.
1024        Requires confidential-client credentials (§12.1 note 4). A ``401``
1025        here is a client-credential failure surfaced as
1026        ``OAuthProtocolError``; it never enters the §9 single-flight
1027        refresh guard (a client-credential failure is not a session
1028        expiry)."""
1029        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
1030        form = self._introspect_form(token=token, token_type_hint=token_type_hint)
1031        url = self._endpoint_url_for_introspect(config, tenant_id)
1032        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1033        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1034        return self._handle_introspect_response(response)
