1036    async def revoke(
1037        self,
1038        *,
1039        token: SecretStr | str,
1040        token_type_hint: str | None = None,
1041        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1042        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1043    ) -> None:
1044        """``POST /oauth2/revoke`` (RFC 7009, CONTRACT.md §12.1) — revoke
1045        an access or refresh token. Idempotent: any ``200`` (including for
1046        a token the server has never seen) is success (§12.1 note 5); only
1047        a ``401`` (client authentication failed) is an error."""
1048        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
1049        form = self._revoke_form(token=token, token_type_hint=token_type_hint)
1050        url = self._endpoint_url_for_revoke(config, tenant_id)
1051        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1052        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1053        self._handle_revoke_response(response)
1054
1055    async def sso_start(
1056        self,
1057        *,
1058        federation_config_id: str,
1059        redirect_uri: str,
1060        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1061        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1062        org_id: str | None = None,
1063        org_slug: str | None = None,
1064    ) -> SsoStartResult:
1065        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oidc/start`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1)
1066        — step 1 of first-time SSO against an upstream IdP. One tenant
1067        form and one org form must be resolvable, from the arguments or
1068        from the client's construction-time/resolved context (§5.1)."""
1069        body = self._sso_start_body(
1070            federation_config_id=federation_config_id,
1071            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1072            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1073            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1074            org_id=org_id,
1075            org_slug=org_slug,
1076        )
1077        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", SSO_START_PATH, json=body)
1078        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1079        return self._handle_sso_start_response(response)
1080
1081    async def sso_complete(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1082        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oidc/callback`` (CONTRACT.md
1083        §12.1) — step 2 of upstream SSO: consumes the single-use ``state``,
1084        provisions or links the user, and establishes the session via
1085        ``Set-Cookie`` (§4 cookie jar). §12.4 does not apply here — no ID
1086        token ever reaches the SDK on the federation path."""
1087        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1088            "POST", SSO_CALLBACK_PATH, json={"state": state, "code": code}
1089        )
1090        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1091        return self._handle_sso_complete_response(response)
1092
1093    async def sso_providers(
1094        self,
1095        *,
1096        org_id: str | None = None,
1097        org_slug: str | None = None,
1098        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1099        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1100    ) -> FederationProviderList:
1101        """``GET /api/v1/auth/federation/providers`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1102        which "Sign in with X" buttons to render for a workspace.
1103
1104        The identifiers travel as **query** parameters; this is a ``GET``
1105        and sends no body.
1106
1107        **An empty list is a success.** An unknown organization, a known one
1108        with nothing configured, and a request naming no workspace at all
1109        all answer ``200`` with an empty ``providers`` array (§12.1 note 9).
1110        Every one of them comes back as an ordinary result, and nothing here
1111        synthesises a not-found: the endpoint is deliberately shaped so it
1112        cannot be used to enumerate organization or tenant slugs, and an SDK
1113        that reintroduced the distinction would reintroduce the oracle. A
1114        caller learns it named the workspace wrongly at the start
1115        operations, where every failure is a uniform ``401``.
1116
1117        For the same reason this is the one federation operation that does
1118        **not** refuse client-side when no workspace resolves.
1119        """
1120        params = self._sso_providers_params(
1121            org_id=org_id,
1122            org_slug=org_slug,
1123            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1124            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1125        )
1126        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("GET", SSO_PROVIDERS_PATH, params=params)
1127        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1128        return self._handle_sso_providers_response(response)
1129
1130    async def sso_start_oauth2(
1131        self,
1132        *,
1133        federation_config_id: str,
1134        redirect_uri: str,
1135        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1136        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1137        org_id: str | None = None,
1138        org_slug: str | None = None,
1139    ) -> SsoStartResult:
1140        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/start`` (CONTRACT.md
1141        §12.1) — step 1 of a login through a **plain-OAuth2** upstream
1142        (GitHub, Facebook, ``generic_oauth2``).
1143
1144        Call this, rather than :meth:`sso_start`, exactly when the
1145        provider's ``protocol`` is ``OAuth2`` (§12.1 note 10). The server
1146        refuses a mismatch with ``400`` rather than accepting it silently,
1147        so a client that assumes OIDC fails on every GitHub button.
1148
1149        PKCE is mandatory on this path and is generated and stored
1150        **server-side**; nothing about it appears in the request or the
1151        response (§12.1 note 11).
1152
1153        A ``400`` here can mean the ``redirect_uri`` is not on an origin the
1154        deployment accepts (§12.1 rule 12a); it surfaces as
1155        :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` and is not retried.
1156        """
1157        body = self._sso_start_oauth2_body(
1158            federation_config_id=federation_config_id,
1159            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1160            tenant_id=tenant_id,
1161            tenant_slug=tenant_slug,
1162            org_id=org_id,
1163            org_slug=org_slug,
1164        )
1165        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", SSO_OAUTH2_START_PATH, json=body)
1166        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1167        return self._handle_sso_start_oauth2_response(response)
1168
1169    async def sso_complete_oauth2(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1170        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oauth2/callback`` (CONTRACT.md
1171        §12.1) — step 2 of a plain-OAuth2 login.
1172
1173        The session arrives as ``Set-Cookie`` (§12.1 note 6) and is absorbed
1174        exactly as :meth:`sso_complete` absorbs it, so ``refresh()`` and
1175        ``logout()`` work afterwards.
1176
1177        §12.4 does not apply: an ``OAuth2`` provider issues no ID token, so
1178        there is nothing to validate. The server authenticated the user by
1179        calling a configured userinfo endpoint with the access token it had
1180        just received — configuration and transport trust rather than
1181        cryptographic trust (§12.1 note 11).
1182        """
1183        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1184            "POST", SSO_OAUTH2_CALLBACK_PATH, json={"state": state, "code": code}
1185        )
1186        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1187        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteOauth2")
1188
1189    async def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1190        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/handoff`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1191        redeem the single-use code the SAML and Apple flows deliver.
1192
1193        Those two protocols return **cross-site**, so the server cannot set
1194        ``SameSite=Strict`` session cookies on that response. It instead
1195        redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an
1196        ``axiam_handoff`` query parameter (``HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM``); this
1197        call posts that code back same-origin, and *this* response is the
1198        one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).
1199
1200        **The code is gone either way.** It is valid for
1201        ``HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`` seconds and redeemable **once**. Redeem
1202        it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed
1203        redemption: a ``401`` is terminal, and this method makes exactly one
1204        wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown,
1205        expired and already-redeemed all answer the same ``401``,
1206        deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to
1207        do.
1208        """
1209        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1210            "POST", SSO_HANDOFF_PATH, json={"code": code}
1211        )
1212        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1213        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteHandoff")
1214
1215    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1216    # §24 WebAuthn / passkeys — the relying-party layer (async twins)
1217    #
1218    # Python has no authenticator, so §24.6b's linked-API helper is
1219    # deliberately absent: §24.6b rule 2 forbids emulating one in software,
1220    # and a "credential" held in process memory is not a second factor. What
1221    # is here is the half that talks to AXIAM, plus §24.6a's JSON bridge —
1222    # which is what lets a Python service be the relying party for a ceremony
1223    # a handset ran.
1224    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1225
1226    async def webauthn_register_start(self) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1227        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1228
1229        Requires a session — enrolling a passkey is something a signed-in user
1230        does to their own account — and refuses **client-side with no wire
1231        call** when there is none.
1232
1233        A ``503`` means the tenant's attestation policy requires attestation
1234        and the FIDO metadata service has no usable snapshot. That is a server
1235        configuration state, not a transient failure, so §24.4 rule 2
1236        deliberately does **not** retry it.
1237        """
1238        self._ensure_open()
1239        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_start")
1240        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._WA_REGISTER_START, json={})
1241        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1242        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_register_start")
1243
1244    async def webauthn_register_finish(
1245        self,
1246        *,
1247        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1248        credential_name: str,
1249        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1250    ) -> WebauthnCredential:
1251        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1252
1253        ``response`` is either the parsed authenticator answer or the
1254        platform's own JSON string (§24.6a rule 2) — Android's
1255        ``registrationResponseJson``, a browser's ``credential.toJSON()``. It
1256        reaches the server unchanged either way: it is the input to a
1257        signature check over bytes this SDK did not produce.
1258        """
1259        self._ensure_open()
1260        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_finish")
1261        body = self._webauthn_register_finish_body(state_token, credential_name, response)
1262        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1263            "POST", self._WA_REGISTER_FINISH, json=body
1264        )
1265        return self._webauthn_credential(await self._rest_send_async(request))
1266
1267    async def webauthn_authenticate_start(
1268        self, *, challenge_token: SecretStr | str
1269    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1270        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1271
1272        The **second-factor** ceremony: it continues a ``login()`` that
1273        answered ``mfa_required`` with ``"webauthn"`` among its methods, and
1274        ``challenge_token`` is that result's ``mfa_token``.
1275
1276        A different flow from :meth:`webauthn_discoverable_start`, not the same
1277        one with an optional argument — see §24.2 for why they cannot be
1278        merged.
1279        """
1280        self._ensure_open()
1281        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1282            "POST", self._WA_AUTH_START, json={"challenge_token": _expose_token(challenge_token)}
1283        )
1284        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1285        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_authenticate_start")
1286
1287    async def webauthn_authenticate_finish(
1288        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1289    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1290        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1291
1292        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3 rule 1). That is not §14.3's
1293        "MAY adopt" posture: ``device_login`` mints tokens a caller may want to
1294        route elsewhere, and this is the SDK's own primary authentication —
1295        returning a token set without adopting it would make a passkey sign-in
1296        the one way to log in that does not log you in.
1297        """
1298        return await self._webauthn_finish_async(
1299            self._WA_AUTH_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_authenticate_finish"
1300        )
1301
1302    async def webauthn_discoverable_start(
1303        self, *, workspace: WebauthnWorkspace | None = None
1304    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1305        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1306
1307        The **primary-factor** ceremony: nothing precedes it, the server sends
1308        an empty ``allowCredentials``, and the assertion itself identifies the
1309        user. The workspace still has to be named — a discoverable credential
1310        is resolved inside one tenant — but it comes from this client's own
1311        configuration unless overridden, and slugs are accepted.
1312        """
1313        self._ensure_open()
1314        body = self._webauthn_discoverable_body(workspace)
1315        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1316            "POST", self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_START, json=body
1317        )
1318        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1319        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_discoverable_start")
1320
1321    async def webauthn_discoverable_finish(
1322        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1323    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1324        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1325
1326        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3). Unlike its username-bound
1327        twin, this fires the server's ``login.post_auth`` reactor hook (§22.5):
1328        there was no password step for the event to have been fired at.
1329        """
1330        return await self._webauthn_finish_async(
1331            self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_discoverable_finish"
1332        )
1333
1334    async def _webauthn_finish_async(
1335        self,
1336        path: str,
1337        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1338        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1339        operation: str,
1340    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1341        """The shared tail of both authentication ceremonies."""
1342        self._ensure_open()
1343        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
1344        # this call changes the subject.
1345        self._on_credential_change()
1346        body = self._webauthn_finish_body(state_token, response, operation)
1347        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
1348        http_response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1349        result = self._webauthn_login_result(http_response, operation)
1350        # The server sets the same axiam_access/axiam_refresh/axiam_csrf triple
1351        # here as it does on a password login, so adoption is the same call.
1352        self._absorb_session_cookies()
1353        return result
1354
1355    async def webauthn_setup_register_start(
1356        self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str
1357    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1358        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/setup/register/start`` (CONTRACT.md
1359        §24.1, §25.2 rule 2 — contract 1.45).
1360
1361        Enrols a passkey or security key as the account's **first** factor
1362        during the forced enrolment ``login()`` demanded — the WebAuthn twin
1363        of :meth:`mfa_setup_enroll`. Takes **no session**: the setup token
1364        from ``login()``'s ``mfa_setup_required`` outcome is the only
1365        credential, and it travels in the body. Unlike
1366        :meth:`webauthn_register_start`, this does **not** call the
1367        require-session guard and does **not** attach this client's own
1368        session credential — even one already configured (§24.8).
1369        """
1370        self._ensure_open()
1371        request = self._session._credential_free_request(
1372            "POST",
1373            self._WA_SETUP_REGISTER_START,
1374            self._webauthn_setup_register_start_body(setup_token),
1375        )
1376        response = await self._session._send_async_credential_free(request)
1377        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_setup_register_start")
1378
1379    async def webauthn_setup_register_finish(
1380        self,
1381        *,
1382        setup_token: SecretStr | str,
1383        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1384        credential_name: str,
1385        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1386    ) -> LoginResult:
1387        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/setup/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md
1388        §24.1, §25.2 rule 2 — contract 1.45).
1389
1390        Completes the login ``login()`` interrupted, exactly as
1391        :meth:`mfa_setup_confirm` does for TOTP: adopts credentials on success
1392        (§24.3's five rules apply verbatim, per §25.2 rule 2) and clears the
1393        §17 decision memo because the subject changed. Takes no session, for
1394        the same reason :meth:`webauthn_setup_register_start` does not — a
1395        second credential on a call whose only credential is meant to be the
1396        setup token invites a server that changes its mind about which to
1397        trust.
1398
1399        A ``403`` here is the tenant's attestation policy refusing **this
1400        authenticator** — an AAGUID that is not allow-listed, a missing FIDO
1401        certification, a revoked status — and its message is surfaced
1402        verbatim (§24.4 rule 1): it is the only way the person holding the
1403        key learns that a different one would work.
1404        """
1405        self._ensure_open()
1406        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
1407        # this call changes the subject.
1408        self._on_credential_change()
1409        body = self._webauthn_setup_register_finish_body(
1410            setup_token, state_token, credential_name, response
1411        )
1412        request = self._session._credential_free_request(
1413            "POST", self._WA_SETUP_REGISTER_FINISH, body
1414        )
1415        http_response = await self._session._send_async_credential_free(request)
1416        return self._handle_setup_register_finish_response(http_response)
1417
1418    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1419    # §25 Account lifecycle and MFA enrolment (async twins)
1420    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1421
1422    async def mfa_enroll(self) -> MfaEnrollment:
1423        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
1424        voluntary TOTP enrolment for the signed-in user.
1425
1426        Changes nothing about the current session. In particular it does
1427        **not** clear the §17 decision memo: the subject has not changed, and
1428        discarding a warm memo on an unrelated profile action costs a round
1429        trip on every check that follows (§25.2 rule 3).
1430        """
1431        self._ensure_open()
1432        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_MFA_ENROLL, json={})
1433        return self._mfa_enrollment(await self._rest_send_async(request), "mfa_enroll")
1434
1435    async def mfa_confirm(self, *, totp_code: str) -> bool:
1436        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — activate the
1437        factor :meth:`mfa_enroll` offered."""
1438        self._ensure_open()
1439        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1440            "POST", self._AC_MFA_CONFIRM, json={"totp_code": totp_code}
1441        )
1442        return self._mfa_confirmed(await self._rest_send_async(request))
1443
1444    async def mfa_setup_enroll(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str) -> MfaEnrollment:
1445        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
1446        the enrolment a ``login()`` demanded.
1447
1448        Reached when ``login()`` returns ``mfa_setup_required``: the tenant
1449        requires MFA and this account has none. There is no session yet — the
1450        setup token *is* the credential.
1451        """
1452        self._ensure_open()
1453        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1454            "POST", self._AC_MFA_SETUP_ENROLL, json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token)}
1455        )
1456        return self._mfa_enrollment(await self._rest_send_async(request), "mfa_setup_enroll")
1457
1458    async def mfa_setup_confirm(
1459        self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str, totp_code: str
1460    ) -> LoginResult:
1461        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — finish
1462        forced enrolment and, with it, the login that was interrupted.
1463
1464        Adopts credentials exactly as ``login()`` does, because it *is* the
1465        completion of a login (§25.2 rule 2).
1466        """
1467        self._ensure_open()
1468        self._on_credential_change()
1469        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1470            "POST",
1471            self._AC_MFA_SETUP_CONFIRM,
1472            json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token), "totp_code": totp_code},
1473        )
1474        return self._handle_login_response(await self._rest_send_async(request))
1475
1476    async def verify_email(self, *, token: SecretStr | str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
1477        """``POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1).
1478
1479        Unauthenticated: a user whose address is unverified may have no session
1480        at all. ``tenant_id`` is a **body** field here — this is not an
1481        ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint, so §12.1 rule 2's query-parameter convention
1482        does not reach it.
1483        """
1484        self._ensure_open()
1485        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1486            "POST",
1487            self._AC_VERIFY_EMAIL,
1488            json={"token": _expose_token(token), "tenant_id": tenant_id},
1489        )
1490        self._expect_no_content(await self._rest_send_async(request), "verify_email")
1491
1492    async def resend_verification(self, *, email: str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
1493        """``POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the
1494        **unauthenticated** resend, for a caller with no session.
1495
1496        **Returns normally whatever the outcome.** The address may not exist,
1497        may already be verified, or may be over the daily limit, and this
1498        answers identically in all of them, because it takes an address from an
1499        anonymous caller and anything else is an oracle for which addresses have
1500        accounts (§25.7).
1501
1502        A caller that *is* signed in wants :meth:`resend_own_verification`,
1503        which says which of those happened. Do not reach for this one because it
1504        is the name you already knew.
1505        """
1506        self._ensure_open()
1507        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1508            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_VERIFICATION, json={"email": email, "tenant_id": tenant_id}
1509        )
1510        self._expect_no_content(await self._rest_send_async(request), "resend_verification")
1511
1512    async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1513        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1514        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1515        and say what happened.
1516
1517        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1518        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1519        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1520        address.
1521
1522        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
1523        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1524        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1525
1526        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1527          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1528          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1529          succeeding.
1530        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1531          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1532        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1533
1534        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1535        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1536        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1537        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1538        """
1539        self._ensure_open()
1540        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1541            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1542        )
1543        self._expect_no_content(await self._rest_send_async(request), "resend_own_verification")
1544
1545    async def request_password_reset(
1546        self,
1547        *,
1548        email: str,
1549        org_slug: str | None = None,
1550        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1551        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1552    ) -> None:
1553        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — ask for a reset
1554        mail.
1555
1556        **Returns normally whether or not the address exists**, and this SDK
1557        exposes no way to tell the two apart. That is not an omission to
1558        improve on: a client that surfaced a "no such user" state — even one
1559        inferred from timing — would turn the endpoint into the account
1560        enumeration oracle its uniform response exists to prevent (§25.4).
1561        """
1562        self._ensure_open()
1563        body = self._password_reset_body(
1564            email=email, org_slug=org_slug, tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_slug=tenant_slug
1565        )
1566        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_RESET, json=body)
1567        self._expect_no_content(await self._rest_send_async(request), "request_password_reset")
1568
1569    async def password_reset_context(self, *, token: SecretStr | str) -> PasswordResetContext:
1570        """``GET /api/v1/auth/reset/context`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the OPAQUE
1571        policy for the account a reset token belongs to.
1572
1573        Call this before :meth:`confirm_password_reset` on any tenant that
1574        might have §23 enabled: the client has to build a registration record,
1575        and building one needs parameters it cannot know before it has a token
1576        to ask with. Sending a plaintext password to a tenant in
1577        ``opaque_mode: required`` is refused, and refused late (§25.4 rule 1).
1578        """
1579        self._ensure_open()
1580        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1581            "GET", self._AC_RESET_CONTEXT, params={"token": _expose_token(token)}
1582        )
1583        return self._reset_context(await self._rest_send_async(request))
1584
1585    async def confirm_password_reset(
1586        self,
1587        *,
1588        token: SecretStr | str,
1589        new_password: SecretStr | str,
1590        tenant_id: str,
1591        opaque: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
1592    ) -> None:
1593        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1)."""
1594        self._ensure_open()
1595        body = self._password_reset_confirm_body(
1596            token=token, new_password=new_password, tenant_id=tenant_id, opaque=opaque
1597        )
1598        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1599            "POST", self._AC_RESET_CONFIRM, json=body
1600        )
1601        self._expect_no_content(await self._rest_send_async(request), "confirm_password_reset")

The AXIAM SDK's dedicated async REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10, SDK-Q08).

await client.login(...) returns a typed ~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult with mfa_required (SC#1) — the same contract as the sync ~axiam_sdk.AxiamClient, on its own dedicated async object. Constructing both an AxiamClient and an AsyncAxiamClient against the same base_url/tenant_slug gives each its own independent _Session (cookie jar, CSRF state, refresh guard) — the two classes do NOT share session state with each other, only each shares consistently within its own sync or async call path.

async def aclose(self) -> None: 
117    async def aclose(self) -> None:
118        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
119
120        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
121        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
122
123        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
124        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
125        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
126        restart and resume; an ``aclose()`` that logged out would silently end
127        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
128        ending the session is what you want.
129
130        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
131        rather than silently reconnecting.
132        """
133        self._closed = True
134        self._decision_memo.clear()
135        await self._session.aclose()

async def login_opaque( self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult: 
202    async def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
203        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
204
205        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.login_opaque`; see that method for
206        the full contract — including what the ``login/start`` response's
207        ``mode`` field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under
208        ``"optional"`` this retries over :meth:`login` and returns that call's
209        outcome, and under ``"required"``, an unrecognised value or no ``mode``
210        at all it raises :class:`AuthError` and retries nothing. Returns the
211        same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
212        ``mfa_required`` case.
213
214        The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it:
215        Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a
216        server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in
217        :func:`asyncio.to_thread`.
218        """
219        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
220
221        self._ensure_open()
222        self._on_credential_change()
223
224        exchange = start_login(password)
225
226        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
227            "POST",
228            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
229            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
230        )
231        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
232        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
233            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
234        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
235
236        try:
237            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
238        except AuthError:
239            # §23.4 rule 7, decided identically to the sync client — the shared
240            # `allows_password_fallback` is what keeps the two from drifting.
241            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
242                raise
243            return await self.login(username_or_email, password)
244
245        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
246            "POST",
247            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
248            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
249        )
250        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
251        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
252            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
253        return self._handle_login_response(response)

OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.

The async twin of AxiamClient.login_opaque(); see that method for the full contract — including what the login/start response's mode field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under "optional" this retries over login() and returns that call's outcome, and under "required", an unrecognised value or no mode at all it raises AuthError and retries nothing. Returns the same LoginResult as login(), including the mfa_required case.

The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it: Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in asyncio.to_thread().

async def refresh(self) -> None: 
321    async def refresh(self) -> None:
322        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
323        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
324        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
325        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
326        self._ensure_open()
327        self._on_credential_change()
328        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
329        if not observed_access:
330            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
331
332        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
333        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
334        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
335        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
336        await self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_async(
337            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_async(tenant_id, org_id)
338        )

359    async def logout(self) -> None:

async def check_access( self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None, *, subject_id: str | None = None) -> AccessResult: 
381    async def check_access(
382        self,
383        action: str,
384        resource_id: str,
385        scope: str | None = None,
386        *,
387        subject_id: str | None = None,
388    ) -> AccessResult:
389        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
390
391        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
392        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
393        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
394        declarative ``require_access`` helper (§11) passes to check the
395        *request's* authenticated user rather than this client's own
396        (often service-account) session.
397        """
398        self._ensure_open()
399        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
400        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
401        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id, self._acting_tenant)
402        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
403        if memoized is not None:
404            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
405            return memoized
406
407        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
408        wire = await self._authz_post_async(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
409        result = AccessResult(**wire)
410
411        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
412        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
413        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
414        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
415        return result

async def oidc_par( self, *, request: AuthorizationRequest, redirect_uri: str, scope: str | list[str] | None = None, dpop_jkt: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest: 
538    async def oidc_par(
539        self,
540        *,
541        request: AuthorizationRequest,
542        redirect_uri: str,
543        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
544        dpop_jkt: str | None = None,
545        tenant_id: str | None = None,
546        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
547    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
548        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
549        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
550        with.
551
552        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
553        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
554        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
555        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
556        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
557        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
558
559        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
560        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
561        authorize any other way (§21.1).
562
563        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
564        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
565
566        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
567        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
568        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
569        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
570
571        ``dpop_jkt`` (RFC 9449 §10.1) binds the authorization code this push
572        will produce to a DPoP key before the browser ever sees a redirect, so
573        the code cannot be exchanged by whoever intercepts it. Pass the RFC
574        7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key the token request will prove
575        possession of; :func:`axiam_sdk._dpop.jwk_thumbprint_s256` computes it
576        from a JWK. It is caller-supplied rather than derived because this SDK
577        holds no DPoP key of its own (§21.9): it verifies proofs, it does not
578        mint them. Omitted from the form entirely when ``None``.
579
580        Raises:
581            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
582                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
583            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
584        """
585        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
586        form = self._par_form(
587            request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope, dpop_jkt=dpop_jkt
588        )
589        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
590        http_request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
591        response = await self._rest_send_async(http_request)
592        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)

POST /oauth2/par (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect with.

PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting scope, redirect_uri, state and the PKCE challenge into a URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque request_uri in the redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that cannot be edited into meaning something else.

Required for a FAPI 2.0 client — profile: "fapi2" refuses a registration that does not set require_par, so such a client cannot authorize any other way (§21.1).

A §12 extension, not a replacement: oidc_exchange afterwards is unchanged, and takes the code_verifier carried on the result.

Not retried on a 5xx or a transport failure — it is a POST that creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only eligibility exactly as oidc_exchange does. The safe recovery is a fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).

dpop_jkt (RFC 9449 §10.1) binds the authorization code this push will produce to a DPoP key before the browser ever sees a redirect, so the code cannot be exchanged by whoever intercepts it. Pass the RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key the token request will prove possession of; axiam_sdk._dpop.jwk_thumbprint_s256() computes it from a JWK. It is caller-supplied rather than derived because this SDK holds no DPoP key of its own (§21.9): it verifies proofs, it does not mint them. Omitted from the form entirely when None.

Raises: AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint. OAuthProtocolError: on any error the server returns.

async def oidc_refresh( self, *, refresh_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
620    async def oidc_refresh(
621        self,
622        *,
623        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
624        scope: str | None = None,
625        tenant_id: str | None = None,
626        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
627    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
628        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
629        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
630
631        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
632        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
633        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
634        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
635        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
636        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
637        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
638        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
639        interleave.
640        """
641
642        async def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
643            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
644            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_async`
645            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
646            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
647            config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
648            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
649            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
650            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
651            response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
652            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
653            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
654
655        async def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
656            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
657            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
658            :meth:`refresh` call."""
659            token_set: OidcTokenSet = await self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_async(
660                do_refresh
661            )
662            return token_set
663
664        result: OidcTokenSet = await self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_async.run(under_guard)
665        return result

async def device_login( self, on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]], *, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
740    async def device_login(
741        self,
742        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]],
743        *,
744        scope: str | None = None,
745        tenant_id: str | None = None,
746        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
747    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
748        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
749        user code, poll to completion.
750
751        ``on_user_code`` is invoked — and **awaited when it returns an
752        awaitable** — before the first poll (§14.3 rule 2). A device rendering
753        a QR code may need to await a paint, and polling before that resolves
754        would defeat the rule as surely as not calling back at all.
755
756        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
757        set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync
758        twin's docstring for the full rule set.
759        """
760        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
761        authorization = await self.device_authorize(
762            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
763        )
764
765        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
766        result = on_user_code(authorization)
767        if isinstance(result, Awaitable):
768            await result
769
770        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
771        while True:
772            if not schedule.tick():
773                raise self._device_expired_error()
774            await asyncio.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
775            try:
776                return await self.device_poll(
777                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
778                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
779                    configuration=config,
780                )
781            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
782                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
783                if outcome in ("pending", "retry"):
784                    continue
785                if outcome == "slow_down":
786                    schedule.slow_down()
787                    continue
788                raise

Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK returns the token set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync twin's docstring for the full rule set.

async def uma_exchange_ticket( self, *, ticket: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, claim_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> RequestingPartyToken: 
928    async def uma_exchange_ticket(
929        self,
930        *,
931        ticket: SecretStr | str,
932        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
933        tenant_id: str | None = None,
934        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
935    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
936        """Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.uma_exchange_ticket`.
937
938        ``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a
939        ticket for an RPT.
940
941        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
942        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
943        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
944        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
945        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second
946        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
947        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On
948        failure, request a **new** ticket.
949
950        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
951
952        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
953          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
954          resource server instead of for the user.
955        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
956          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
957          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
958        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
959          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
960          that user.
961
962        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
963        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
964        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
965        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
966
967        Raises:
968            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
969                with no wire call.
970        """
971        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
972        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
973        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
974        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
975        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
976        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)

POST /oauth2/token with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a ticket for an RPT.

This method never retries. It issues exactly one request and is outside the §16 retry policy — not on 5xx, not on timeout, not on any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed before the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a new ticket.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default claim_token (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the resource server instead of for the user.
  • No auto-narrowing on access_denied (rule 3). A partial grant is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the application's judgement, not this SDK's.
  • No adoption (rule 4). The RPT is the requesting party's token. Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as that user.

The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client — all answer invalid_grant with one message. This SDK does not try to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller cannot probe for live ticket handles.

Raises: AuthError: when no client_secret was configured — client-side, with no wire call.

async def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult: 
1189    async def sso_complete_handoff(self, *, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1190        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/handoff`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1191        redeem the single-use code the SAML and Apple flows deliver.
1192

1194        ``SameSite=Strict`` session cookies on that response. It instead
1195        redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an
1196        ``axiam_handoff`` query parameter (``HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM``); this
1197        call posts that code back same-origin, and *this* response is the
1198        one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).
1199
1200        **The code is gone either way.** It is valid for
1201        ``HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS`` seconds and redeemable **once**. Redeem
1202        it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed
1203        redemption: a ``401`` is terminal, and this method makes exactly one
1204        wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown,
1205        expired and already-redeemed all answer the same ``401``,
1206        deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to
1207        do.
1208        """
1209        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1210            "POST", SSO_HANDOFF_PATH, json={"code": code}
1211        )
1212        response = await self._rest_send_async(request)
1213        return self._handle_federation_session_response(response, "ssoCompleteHandoff")

It instead redirects the browser to the SPA's callback URL with an axiam_handoff query parameter (HANDOFF_QUERY_PARAM); this call posts that code back same-origin, and this response is the one that carries the cookies (§12.1 note 12).

The code is gone either way. It is valid for HANDOFF_CODE_TTL_SECONDS seconds and redeemable once. Redeem it from the same origin, immediately, and never retry a failed redemption: a 401 is terminal, and this method makes exactly one wire call so that it cannot become a retry by accident. Unknown, expired and already-redeemed all answer the same 401, deliberately — telling them apart is not something a caller gets to do.

1388        §24.1, §25.2 rule 2 — contract 1.45).

1391        :meth:`mfa_setup_confirm` does for TOTP: adopts credentials on success

1393        §17 decision memo because the subject changed. Takes no session, for

async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None: 
1512    async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1513        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1514        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1515        and say what happened.
1516
1517        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1518        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1519        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1520        address.

1523        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1524        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1525
1526        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1527          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1528          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1529          succeeding.
1530        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1531          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1532        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1533
1534        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1535        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1536        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1537        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1538        """
1539        self._ensure_open()
1540        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1541            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1542        )

POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification (CONTRACT.md §25.1, §25.7) — resend the signed-in caller's own verification mail, and say what happened.

Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary address.

Unlike resend_verification() this reports the outcome, because the caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:

  • returns — a token was minted and the mail enqueued. Delivery is asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this succeeding.
  • ~axiam_sdk.ConflictError (from 409) — already verified, or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
  • ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError (from 429) — the daily limit.

§25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.

 40    #: which completes this login.

 52    """Whether the account that just signed in is an **organization-level**
 53    principal — CONTRACT.md §5.2.
 54
 55    Such a principal's record lives in its organization's reserved tenant, so
 56    its global grants apply in every tenant of that organization, and it can act
 57    on a different one by sending a different ``X-Axiam-Tenant`` on the next
 58    request — no re-login, because it already is a principal of every tenant
 59    there.
 60

 62    the header for one of those produces a ``403``, so this flag is what an

 77

 81

 83    registration record for *this* account must be sealed against — see

Since contract 1.35 that reach can be narrowed per assignment, so this flag alone no longer decides what to offer: consult reachable_tenant_ids as well (§5.2.3 rule 3).

principal_tenant_id: str | None = None

The tenant this principal's record lives in — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2.

Distinct from the tenant a request acts on: the two are the same value for every ordinary principal and diverge only once an organization-level one selects another tenant.

This is where the account's own credentials belong, and what a §23 registration record for this account must be sealed against — see AxiamClient.opaque_enrollment_for_self.

Falls back to the acting tenant the server reported when it omits this, which is exactly right there: a server older than contract 1.34 cannot switch the acting tenant, so the two cannot differ.

principal_tenant_slug: str | None = None

Slug of principal_tenant_id — "organization" for an organization-level principal. None when the server omits it.

org_id: str | None = None

The caller's organization as a UUID — CONTRACT.md §5.2.2 rule 3.

Read this rather than resolving a slug through GET /api/v1/organizations, which is super-admin-only and returns only the caller's own organization.

reachable_tenant_ids: tuple[str, ...] | None = None

The tenants this caller's roles reach, when narrowed — CONTRACT.md §5.2.3.

None means unrestricted, which is both the common case and the only thing a server older than contract 1.35 can mean. A present tuple is a deliberately narrowed organization-level account: confine any tenant switch to it, because naming anything outside is refused at the header (§5.2.3 rule 4).

Note the pairing with organization_level: a narrowed account still reports True there, so gating on that flag alone offers tenants the server will refuse.

250@dataclass(frozen=True)
251class UmaChallenger:
252    """A configured ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA`` challenge emitter (§20.3, emit half).
253
254    Hand one to :func:`axiam_sdk.fastapi.require_access` (or Django's
255    ``@require_access``) and a denial stops being a bare 403: the guard mints a
256    fresh permission ticket for the pairs the caller lacked and returns it in
257    the header, so a UMA-aware client knows where to go for authority instead of
258    only being told "no".
259
260    **Opt-in, and deliberately so.** Emitting a challenge means minting a
261    credential — a wire call to the Protection API, and a live ticket, produced
262    on a path the caller did not explicitly request. A guard that did that on
263    every denial by default would turn each unauthorized request into a
264    Protection API call, which is a denial-of-service amplifier pointed at your
265    own authorization server.
266
267    **Failure is not escalation.** If minting fails — the PAT expired, the
268    Protection API is down, the resource declares none of the requested scopes —
269    the denial still surfaces as an ordinary 403 without a challenge. A caller
270    who was going to be refused is refused either way; letting a Protection API
271    outage turn a deny into a 500 would hand the outage a second consequence,
272    and letting it turn into an allow would be a security bug.
273
274    :param realm: The protection realm to name in the header.
275    :param as_uri: The authorization server to send the caller to — normally
276        this deployment's issuer, read from discovery rather than concatenated
277        by hand.
278    :param pat: A Protection API Token: a *client-credentials* token carrying
279        the ``uma_protection`` scope (§20.2 rule 1). A user token cannot stand
280        in — a minted ticket is bound to the ``client_id`` that minted it.
281    :param client: The client whose ``uma_request_ticket`` mints the ticket.
282        Async guards need the async client; sync guards the sync one.
283    """
284
285    realm: str
286    as_uri: str
287    pat: SecretStr | str
288    client: Any

A configured WWW-Authenticate: UMA challenge emitter (§20.3, emit half).

Hand one to axiam_sdk.fastapi.require_access() (or Django's @require_access) and a denial stops being a bare 403: the guard mints a fresh permission ticket for the pairs the caller lacked and returns it in the header, so a UMA-aware client knows where to go for authority instead of only being told "no".

Opt-in, and deliberately so. Emitting a challenge means minting a credential — a wire call to the Protection API, and a live ticket, produced on a path the caller did not explicitly request. A guard that did that on every denial by default would turn each unauthorized request into a Protection API call, which is a denial-of-service amplifier pointed at your own authorization server.

Failure is not escalation. If minting fails — the PAT expired, the Protection API is down, the resource declares none of the requested scopes — the denial still surfaces as an ordinary 403 without a challenge. A caller who was going to be refused is refused either way; letting a Protection API outage turn a deny into a 500 would hand the outage a second consequence, and letting it turn into an allow would be a security bug.

Parameters
  • realm: The protection realm to name in the header.
  • as_uri: The authorization server to send the caller to — normally this deployment's issuer, read from discovery rather than concatenated by hand.
  • pat: A Protection API Token: a client-credentials token carrying the uma_protection scope (§20.2 rule 1). A user token cannot stand in — a minted ticket is bound to the client_id that minted it.
  • client: The client whose uma_request_ticket mints the ticket. Async guards need the async client; sync guards the sync one.

def uma_parse_challenge(header: str) -> UmaChallenge | None: 
161def uma_parse_challenge(header: str) -> UmaChallenge | None:
162    """Parse a ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA …`` header value (CONTRACT.md §20.3).
163
164    **This deliberately does not exchange the ticket.** Parsing a challenge and
165    acting on it are separate decisions: the ``as_uri`` names an authorization
166    server the caller has not necessarily chosen to trust, and auto-exchanging
167    would send the requesting party's ``claim_token`` to whatever host answered
168    the 403. The caller decides.
169
170    Returns ``None`` when the header is not a UMA challenge.
171    """
172    trimmed = header.strip()
173    if not trimmed.startswith("UMA"):
174        return None
175    rest = trimmed[3:]
176    # "UMA" alone is a valid, if useless, challenge; anything else must be
177    # separated by whitespace so `UMAX realm="…"` is not read as UMA.
178    if rest and not rest[0].isspace():
179        return None
180
181    fields: dict[str, str] = {}
182    for part in rest.split(","):
183        key, sep, value = part.partition("=")
184        if not sep:
185            continue
186        fields[key.strip()] = value.strip().strip('"')
187
188    ticket = fields.get("ticket")
189    return UmaChallenge(
190        realm=fields.get("realm"),
191        as_uri=fields.get("as_uri"),
192        ticket=SecretStr(ticket) if ticket is not None else None,
193    )

Parse a WWW-Authenticate: UMA … header value (CONTRACT.md §20.3).

This deliberately does not exchange the ticket. Parsing a challenge and acting on it are separate decisions: the as_uri names an authorization server the caller has not necessarily chosen to trust, and auto-exchanging would send the requesting party's claim_token to whatever host answered the 403. The caller decides.

Returns None when the header is not a UMA challenge.

def uma_challenge_header(realm: str, as_uri: str, ticket: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str) -> str: 
196def uma_challenge_header(realm: str, as_uri: str, ticket: SecretStr | str) -> str:
197    """Format a ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA`` header value (§20.3, emit half).
198
199    The resource-server side: having obtained a ticket from
200    ``uma_request_ticket``, tell the caller where to redeem it.
201    """
202    return f'UMA realm="{realm}", as_uri="{as_uri}", ticket="{_expose_secret(ticket)}"'

Format a WWW-Authenticate: UMA header value (§20.3, emit half).

The resource-server side: having obtained a ticket from uma_request_ticket, tell the caller where to redeem it.

30class AuthError(Exception):
31    """Authentication failure: wrong credentials, expired session, MFA
32    failure, or a 401 on refresh (CONTRACT.md §2)."""

34    def __init__(self, message: str, reason: str | None = None) -> None:
35        """Build the exception with ``message`` describing the failure
36        (CONTRACT.md §2 construction rule); the exception's own ``str()``
37        prefixes it with ``"authentication failed: "``.
38
39        ``reason`` is an optional stable, machine-readable code (CONTRACT.md
40        §12.3 rule 3 / §12.4) — populated by the OIDC ID-token validation
41        checklist with one of the seven contract-fixed reason codes
42        (``invalid_alg``, ``unknown_kid``, ``invalid_signature``,
43        ``invalid_issuer``, ``invalid_audience``, ``token_expired``,
44        ``nonce_mismatch``); ``None`` for every other ``AuthError``. It is a
45        code, never free text, so callers can branch on it without parsing
46        ``message``.
47        """
48        super().__init__(f"authentication failed: {message}")
49        self.message = message
50        self.reason = reason

111class NetworkError(Exception):
112    """Transport-level failure: connection refused, timeout, TLS error, DNS
113    failure, or a server-side 5xx (CONTRACT.md §2).
114
115    ``cause`` is set as ``__cause__`` for standard Python exception chaining
116    (``raise ... from cause`` semantics). It MUST only ever be populated via
117    ``error_from_http_status``/``error_from_grpc_status``, which redact
118    sensitive headers from any wrapped ``httpx.Response`` BEFORE constructing
119    this error (D-08, CR-04 carry-forward) — never construct this class
120    directly from an unredacted response.
121    """
122
123    def __init__(self, message: str, cause: BaseException | None = None) -> None:
124        """Build the exception with ``message`` and an optional already-
125        redacted ``cause`` (CONTRACT.md §2 construction rule); the
126        exception's own ``str()`` prefixes ``message`` with ``"network
127        error: "``. See the class docstring for the redact-before-wrap
128        invariant governing ``cause``."""
129        super().__init__(f"network error: {message}")
130        self.message = message
131        self.__cause__ = cause

class OAuthProtocolError(axiam_sdk.AuthError): 
53class OAuthProtocolError(AuthError):
54    """An RFC 6749 protocol error returned by an ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint as an
55    ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` body (CONTRACT.md §2 sub-type table, §12.3 rule 3,
56    port-brief-addendum item 17).
57
58    A **sub-type of** :class:`AuthError`, not a fourth peer error type:
59    existing ``except AuthError:`` blocks keep matching it unchanged — that
60    backward compatibility is precisely what makes contract 1.4 "non-breaking,
61    additive". Raised for a ``400`` from ``POST /oauth2/token`` (e.g.
62    ``invalid_grant``) and for a ``401`` from ``POST /oauth2/introspect`` /
63    ``POST /oauth2/revoke`` (client authentication failed) — neither of which
64    may collapse into the generic §2 ``400 -> NetworkError`` / ``401 ->
65    AuthError`` rows.
66
67    ``str(exc)`` is always exactly ``"<error>: <error_description>"``, built
68    from the two ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` wire fields, which are also exposed
69    individually as :attr:`error`/:attr:`error_description`. This
70    deliberately bypasses :class:`AuthError`'s own ``"authentication failed:
71    "`` message-prefixing convention: §12.3 rule 3 fixes this class's message
72    to exactly ``"<error>: <error_description>"``, so ``Exception.__init__``
73    is called directly rather than via ``AuthError.__init__``.
74    """
75
76    def __init__(self, error: str, error_description: str) -> None:
77        """Build the exception from the two ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` wire
78        fields (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 3); ``error``/``error_description``
79        are exposed as public attributes, and ``str(self)`` is exactly
80        ``"<error>: <error_description>"``."""
81        message = f"{error}: {error_description}"
82        Exception.__init__(self, message)
83        self.message = message
84        self.reason = None
85        self.error = error
86        self.error_description = error_description

285class OidcConfiguration(BaseModel):
286    """The OIDC Discovery 1.0 metadata document served by ``GET
287    /.well-known/openid-configuration`` (wire schema ``OidcDiscoveryDocument``,
288    CONTRACT.md §12.1). Every field is required by the server's schema.
289
290    Field names keep their wire (snake_case) spelling deliberately — this
291    IS a protocol document, cross-referenced against OIDC Discovery 1.0 /
292    RFC 8414 by field name, so renaming would be a lossy translation
293    (mirrors ``the TypeScript SDK's src/node/oidcTypes.ts``).
294
295    ``issuer`` is the **authoritative** issuer for ID-token validation
296    (CONTRACT.md §12.4 rule 3). It may legitimately differ from the client's
297    ``base_url`` when AXIAM runs behind a proxy, so this SDK never rejects a
298    document on an issuer/base-URL mismatch (§12.3 rule 6). Likewise
299    ``jwks_uri`` is read from here rather than hardcoded.
300    """
301

235class MtlsEndpointAliases(BaseModel):
236    """RFC 8705 §5 ``mtls_endpoint_aliases`` — the six endpoints re-based on
237    the host that performs the mutual-TLS handshake (wire schema
238    ``MtlsEndpointAliases``, contract 1.40).
239
240    A TLS listener decides whether to request a client certificate during the
241    handshake, before it has seen any HTTP, so "ask for a certificate on
242    ``/oauth2/token`` but not on ``/oauth2/authorize``" is not something one
243    listener can do. A deployment wanting both runs two, and this object names
244    the second.
245
246    Only these six are ever aliased. ``authorization_endpoint`` and
247    ``end_session_endpoint`` are front-channel and ``jwks_uri`` is public key
248    material, so CONTRACT.md §21.3 rule 2 forbids synthesising an alias for any
249    of them — sending a browser to an mTLS host raises a native
250    certificate-chooser dialog most users cannot answer. ``issuer`` is not an
251    endpoint and does not move either: §12.4 rule 3 still compares ``iss``
252    against it by exact string.
253
254    Every field is optional even though the server's schema marks all six
255    required. AXIAM builds them from one path through a shared macro and so
256    always publishes the complete set, but RFC 8705 §5 permits an OP to alias
257    fewer, and the shape of this member must never be why a client stops
258    working — the same principle rule 2 point 1 states for the object as a
259    whole, one level in. An absent entry falls back to the top-level endpoint
260    of the same name, exactly as an absent object does.
261    """
262
263    token_endpoint: str | None = None
264    """RFC 8705 §2 client authentication, and §3 the mint of a
265    certificate-bound token."""
266
267    userinfo_endpoint: str | None = None
268    """OIDC Core §5.3, reached with an access token that may carry ``cnf``."""
269
270    revocation_endpoint: str | None = None
271    """RFC 7009 §2.1 — authenticates the client."""
272
273    introspection_endpoint: str | None = None
274    """RFC 7662 §2.1 — authenticates the caller."""
275
276    device_authorization_endpoint: str | None = None
277    """RFC 8628 §3.1 — authenticates the client."""
278
279    pushed_authorization_request_endpoint: str | None = None
280    """RFC 9126 §2 — authenticates the client."""
281
282    model_config = {"frozen": True}

RFC 8705 §5 mtls_endpoint_aliases — the six endpoints re-based on the host that performs the mutual-TLS handshake (wire schema MtlsEndpointAliases, contract 1.40).

A TLS listener decides whether to request a client certificate during the handshake, before it has seen any HTTP, so "ask for a certificate on /oauth2/token but not on /oauth2/authorize" is not something one listener can do. A deployment wanting both runs two, and this object names the second.

Only these six are ever aliased. authorization_endpoint and end_session_endpoint are front-channel and jwks_uri is public key material, so CONTRACT.md §21.3 rule 2 forbids synthesising an alias for any of them — sending a browser to an mTLS host raises a native certificate-chooser dialog most users cannot answer. issuer is not an endpoint and does not move either: §12.4 rule 3 still compares iss against it by exact string.

Every field is optional even though the server's schema marks all six required. AXIAM builds them from one path through a shared macro and so always publishes the complete set, but RFC 8705 §5 permits an OP to alias fewer, and the shape of this member must never be why a client stops working — the same principle rule 2 point 1 states for the object as a whole, one level in. An absent entry falls back to the top-level endpoint of the same name, exactly as an absent object does.

568    note 13) and this id is how the server is told what resolution
569    produced."""

1771def _no_init_or_replace_init(self, *args, **kwargs):
1772    cls = type(self)
1773
1774    if cls._is_protocol:
1775        raise TypeError('Protocols cannot be instantiated')
1776
1777    # Already using a custom `__init__`. No need to calculate correct
1778    # `__init__` to call. This can lead to RecursionError. See bpo-45121.
1779    if cls.__init__ is not _no_init_or_replace_init:
1780        return
1781
1782    # Initially, `__init__` of a protocol subclass is set to `_no_init_or_replace_init`.
1783    # The first instantiation of the subclass will call `_no_init_or_replace_init` which
1784    # searches for a proper new `__init__` in the MRO. The new `__init__`
1785    # replaces the subclass' old `__init__` (ie `_no_init_or_replace_init`). Subsequent
1786    # instantiation of the protocol subclass will thus use the new
1787    # `__init__` and no longer call `_no_init_or_replace_init`.
1788    for base in cls.__mro__:
1789        init = base.__dict__.get('__init__', _no_init_or_replace_init)
1790        if init is not _no_init_or_replace_init:
1791            cls.__init__ = init
1792            break
1793    else:
1794        # should not happen
1795        cls.__init__ = object.__init__
1796
1797    cls.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs)
