class MemoryOidcStateStore: 
 86class MemoryOidcStateStore:
 87    """In-memory reference implementation of :class:`OidcStateStore`
 88    (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).
 89
 90    Per-instance (never process-global), single-use, 10-minute TTL. Expired
 91    entries are dropped lazily on :meth:`consume` and swept opportunistically
 92    on :meth:`save` — no background thread/timer is held, since a library
 93    must not keep the host process alive (port-brief-addendum item 8).
 94
 95    Suitable for a single-process app and for tests. A multi-instance
 96    deployment needs a shared store (Redis, database) — implement
 97    :class:`OidcStateStore` yourself for that; nothing in the SDK assumes
 98    this class.
 99
100    Thread-safe: guarded by a single ``threading.Lock`` so concurrent sync
101    and async (via ``asyncio``'s default single-threaded event loop, or a
102    thread-pool-offloaded call) callers never corrupt the underlying dict.
103    """
104
105    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float = OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS) -> None:
106        """Build an empty store.
107
108        Args:
109            ttl_seconds: Entry lifetime in seconds. Defaults to
110                :data:`OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS` (10 minutes) and is
111                **clamped to it**: a shorter TTL is honored (useful in
112                tests), a longer one is reduced, because CONTRACT.md §12.3
113                rule 1 fixes 10 minutes as the maximum.
114        """
115        self._ttl_seconds = min(ttl_seconds, OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS)
116        self._entries: dict[str, tuple[OidcStateEntry, float]] = {}
117        self._lock = threading.Lock()
118
119    @property
120    def size(self) -> int:
121        """Number of unexpired entries currently held (tests/metrics)."""
122        with self._lock:
123            self._sweep_locked()
124            return len(self._entries)
125
126    def save(self, entry: OidcStateEntry) -> None:
127        """Persist ``entry`` under its own ``state``, expiring
128        ``ttl_seconds`` from now."""
129        with self._lock:
130            self._sweep_locked()
131            self._entries[entry.state] = (entry, time.monotonic() + self._ttl_seconds)
132
133    def consume(self, state: str) -> OidcStateEntry | None:
134        """Atomically return and delete the entry for ``state``.
135
136        Deletion happens before the expiry check, so even an expired hit is
137        removed rather than left to accumulate, and a second call can never
138        return the same entry twice.
139        """
140        with self._lock:
141            held = self._entries.pop(state, None)
142            if held is None:
143                return None
144            entry, expires_at = held
145            if expires_at <= time.monotonic():
146                return None
147            return entry
148
149    def _sweep_locked(self) -> None:
150        """Drop every expired entry. Caller MUST already hold ``self._lock``.
151        Lazy housekeeping — no background timer."""
152        now = time.monotonic()
153        expired = [
154            state for state, (_entry, expires_at) in self._entries.items() if expires_at <= now
155        ]
156        for state in expired:
157            del self._entries[state]

In-memory reference implementation of OidcStateStore (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).

Suitable for a single-process app and for tests. A multi-instance deployment needs a shared store (Redis, database) — implement OidcStateStore yourself for that; nothing in the SDK assumes this class.

Thread-safe: guarded by a single threading.Lock so concurrent sync and async (via asyncio's default single-threaded event loop, or a thread-pool-offloaded call) callers never corrupt the underlying dict.

def classify_webauthn_error(error: object) -> WebauthnFailure: 
173def classify_webauthn_error(error: object) -> WebauthnFailure:
174    """Map a platform ceremony error to its canonical classification (§24.6b
175    rule 5).
176
177    Accepts anything a caller can get hold of: an exception, an error name
178    relayed from a browser or an Android ``CreateCredentialException``, an
179    ``ASAuthorizationError`` code by name. Everything unrecognized is
180    :attr:`WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN` rather than a raise — a classifier that can
181    fail is one more thing for an error handler to handle.
182    """
183    if isinstance(error, str):
184        name: str | None = error
185    elif isinstance(error, BaseException):
186        name = type(error).__name__
187    else:
188        name = getattr(error, "name", None)
189        if not isinstance(name, str):
190            name = None
191    if name is None:
192        return WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN
193    return _FAILURE_BY_NAME.get(name.strip().lower(), WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN)

200    cancelling: the same classification covers a silent timeout, and the spec
201    will not say which happened.
202    """
203    return _FAILURE_MESSAGES[failure]

def webauthn_request_json( challenge: WebauthnChallenge | dict[str, typing.Any]) -> str: 
206def webauthn_request_json(challenge: WebauthnChallenge | dict[str, Any]) -> str:
207    """The challenge in the JSON form every platform authenticator API takes
208    (§24.6a rule 1).
209
210    This is the string an Android app passes to
211    ``CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest`` or ``GetPublicKeyCredentialOption``,
212    and the value a browser passes to
213    ``PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON()``. It is the inner
214    options object: the ``publicKey`` wrapper belongs to the DOM's
215    ``CredentialCreationOptions`` and the platform JSON APIs do not want it.
216
217    Pure local computation, no I/O. Nothing is defaulted, dropped or reordered
218    on the way through (§24.0).
219    """
220    raw = challenge.challenge if isinstance(challenge, WebauthnChallenge) else challenge
221    return json.dumps(raw.get("publicKey", raw), separators=(",", ":"))

276    resource server's is worse than no challenge at all.
277    """
278
279    #: The RFC 9728 §2 document, ready to serialize.
280    document: ProtectedResourceMetadataDocument
281    #: The absolute path the document is served at, derived from the
282    #: resource per §28.3 — never chosen.
283    metadata_path: str
284    #: :attr:`metadata_path` resolved against the resource's scheme and
285    #: authority. Feed this to the guard's ``resource_metadata_url``.
286    metadata_url: str

What protected_resource_metadata() (and ~axiam_sdk.fastapi.serve_protected_resource_metadata()) return: the document, the path it is served at, and the URL that path resolves to.

metadata_url exists so that an integrator feeds the guard's resource_metadata_url option (§28.5) from the value derived here rather than by retyping the string — retyping is how the two come to disagree, and a challenge pointing at a document that is not this resource server's is worse than no challenge at all.

ProtectedResourceMetadata( document: ProtectedResourceMetadataDocument, metadata_path: str, metadata_url: str)
document: ProtectedResourceMetadataDocument
metadata_path: str
metadata_url: str

class ProtectedResourceMetadataDocument: 
225@dataclass(frozen=True)
226class ProtectedResourceMetadataDocument:
227    """The RFC 9728 §2 document, carrying **at most** the five members §28.2
228    permits, in that order, and no others.
229
230    Two members are **omitted rather than emitted empty or null** by
231    :meth:`to_dict`: ``scopes_supported`` when the caller passed no scopes,
232    and ``resource_documentation`` when the caller passed none.
233    """
234
235    #: The resource identifier this server publishes for itself — the string
236    #: an RFC 8707 ``resource`` parameter carries and the ``aud`` the guard
237    #: checks.
238    resource: str
239    #: The issuer identifiers of the authorization servers that guard this
240    #: resource. At least one, each verbatim.
241    authorization_servers: tuple[str, ...]
242    #: The scope tokens this resource server understands, in the caller's
243    #: order. ``None`` when the caller passed none (member omitted).
244    scopes_supported: tuple[str, ...] | None
245    #: Always ``("header",)`` in this contract version — §10's guard reads a
246    #: bearer credential from the ``Authorization`` header alone.
247    bearer_methods_supported: tuple[str, ...]
248    #: A human-readable documentation page. ``None`` when the caller passed
249    #: none (member omitted; never emitted as ``null``).
250    resource_documentation: str | None
251
252    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
253        """Serialize to the exact JSON shape and member order §28.2 fixes."""
254        document: dict[str, object] = {
255            "resource": self.resource,
256            "authorization_servers": list(self.authorization_servers),
257        }
258        if self.scopes_supported:
259            document["scopes_supported"] = list(self.scopes_supported)
260        document["bearer_methods_supported"] = list(self.bearer_methods_supported)
261        if self.resource_documentation is not None:
262            document["resource_documentation"] = self.resource_documentation
263        return document

def bearer_challenge( resource_metadata_url: str, error: Optional[Literal['invalid_request', 'invalid_token', 'insufficient_scope']] = None, error_description: str | None = None, scope: str | None = None) -> str: 
436def bearer_challenge(
437    resource_metadata_url: str,
438    error: BearerChallengeError | None = None,
439    error_description: str | None = None,
440    scope: str | None = None,
441) -> str:
442    """``bearer_challenge(...)`` (CONTRACT.md §28.4) — build the **value** of
443    a ``WWW-Authenticate`` header, never the whole header line and never a
444    mapping. The caller sets the header.
445
446    Parameters appear in a fixed order — ``error``, ``error_description``,
447    ``scope``, ``resource_metadata`` — separated by exactly ``, ``.
448    ``resource_metadata`` is always present; the other three are omitted
449    when not given.
450
451    **Every value is quoted and no value is ever escaped.** RFC 6750 §3
452    restricts each parameter to a character set that cannot contain ``"`` or
453    ``\\``, so a value needing an escape is a value that does not belong in
454    a challenge: this function refuses it rather than escaping, truncating
455    or stripping it. A challenge is built from the code's own constants and
456    a route's own configuration, so an invalid one is a programming error,
457    not a runtime condition to degrade around.
458
459    Args:
460        resource_metadata_url: The document's URL — the one parameter that
461            is always present. May carry a query and a fragment.
462        error: One of RFC 6750 §3.1's three codes, or ``None`` when the
463            request carried no authentication information at all.
464        error_description: A human-readable description, for an application
465            building **its own** challenge for its own 400. The SDK's own
466            guards never set it: expired, not yet valid, wrong tenant, wrong
467            audience, bad signature, an unsatisfiable ``cnf``, a revoked
468            ``sid`` — §28.4 makes all of them ``invalid_token``,
469            indistinguishably. Every distinction a 401 draws for an
470            unauthenticated stranger is an oracle.
471        scope: The scope the route asked for, verbatim — one or more tokens
472            joined by a single space.
473
474    Returns:
475        The ``WWW-Authenticate`` header value.
476
477    Raises:
478        ValidationError: when any parameter is outside RFC 6750's syntax.
479
480    Example::
481
482        bearer_challenge(metadata.metadata_url)
483        # 'Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"'
484
485        bearer_challenge(metadata.metadata_url, error="insufficient_scope", scope="mcp:tools")
486        # 'Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="mcp:tools", resource_metadata="https://.../mcp"'
487    """
488    op = "bearer_challenge"
489    params: list[str] = []
490
491    if error is not None:
492        if error not in _BEARER_CHALLENGE_ERRORS:
493            _refuse(
494                op,
495                "error",
496                "must be one of invalid_request, invalid_token, insufficient_scope — "
497                f"RFC 6750 §3.1 defines no others, and {error!r} is not among them",
498            )
499        params.append(f'error="{error}"')
500
501    if error_description is not None:
502        if (
503            not isinstance(error_description, str)
504            or error_description == ""
505            or not _is_all(error_description, _is_nqschar)
506        ):
507            _refuse(
508                op,
509                "error_description",
510                "must be one or more NQSCHAR (no '\"', no '\\\\', no control character, "
511                "no non-ASCII) — a value needing an escape does not belong in a challenge",
512            )
513        params.append(f'error_description="{error_description}"')
514
515    if scope is not None:
516        if not isinstance(scope, str) or scope == "":
517            _refuse(op, "scope", "must be one or more scope tokens joined by a single space")
518        for token in scope.split(" "):
519            if token == "" or not _is_all(token, _is_nqchar):
520                _refuse(
521                    op,
522                    "scope",
523                    f"{scope!r} is not a space-joined list of scope tokens — no leading, "
524                    "trailing or doubled space, and no empty token",
525                )
526        params.append(f'scope="{scope}"')
527
528    _require_absolute_uri(op, "resource_metadata", resource_metadata_url, _LOCATOR)
529    if not _is_all(resource_metadata_url, _is_nqchar):
530        _refuse(
531            op,
532            "resource_metadata",
533            "must carry no '\"', no '\\\\', no space and no control character — a "
534            "correctly encoded URL cannot, so one that does has not been encoded",
535        )
536    params.append(f'resource_metadata="{resource_metadata_url}"')
537
538    return f"Bearer {', '.join(params)}"

bearer_challenge(...) (CONTRACT.md §28.4) — build the value of a WWW-Authenticate header, never the whole header line and never a mapping. The caller sets the header.

Parameters appear in a fixed order — error, error_description, scope, resource_metadata — separated by exactly ,. resource_metadata is always present; the other three are omitted when not given.

Every value is quoted and no value is ever escaped. RFC 6750 §3 restricts each parameter to a character set that cannot contain " or \, so a value needing an escape is a value that does not belong in a challenge: this function refuses it rather than escaping, truncating or stripping it. A challenge is built from the code's own constants and a route's own configuration, so an invalid one is a programming error, not a runtime condition to degrade around.

Args: resource_metadata_url: The document's URL — the one parameter that is always present. May carry a query and a fragment. error: One of RFC 6750 §3.1's three codes, or None when the request carried no authentication information at all. error_description: A human-readable description, for an application building its own challenge for its own 400. The SDK's own guards never set it: expired, not yet valid, wrong tenant, wrong audience, bad signature, an unsatisfiable cnf, a revoked sid — §28.4 makes all of them invalid_token, indistinguishably. Every distinction a 401 draws for an unauthenticated stranger is an oracle. scope: The scope the route asked for, verbatim — one or more tokens joined by a single space.

Returns: The WWW-Authenticate header value.

Raises: ValidationError: when any parameter is outside RFC 6750's syntax.

Example::

bearer_challenge(metadata.metadata_url)
# 'Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"'

bearer_challenge(metadata.metadata_url, error="insufficient_scope", scope="mcp:tools")
# 'Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="mcp:tools", resource_metadata="https://.../mcp"'
def protected_resource_metadata( resource: str, authorization_servers: Sequence[str], scopes_supported: Sequence[str], bearer_methods_supported: Sequence[str] = ('header',), resource_documentation: str | None = None) -> ProtectedResourceMetadata: 
300def protected_resource_metadata(
301    resource: str,
302    authorization_servers: Sequence[str],
303    scopes_supported: Sequence[str],
304    bearer_methods_supported: Sequence[str] = ("header",),
305    resource_documentation: str | None = None,
306) -> ProtectedResourceMetadata:
307    """``protected_resource_metadata(...)`` (CONTRACT.md §28.1) — build and
308    validate the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata document this server
309    publishes about itself, and derive the path and URL it is served at.
310
311    **Validation happens here and it refuses; it never repairs.** Every
312    §28.2 rule is checked before any route exists and before any request is
313    served, and a violation raises :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError`'s
314    :class:`~axiam_sdk.management.ValidationError` sub-type. Nothing is
315    normalised, trimmed, lowercased or re-encoded to make it pass: a value
316    that needs adjusting is a configuration mistake an operator fixes in one
317    line, and a helper that quietly fixed it would publish a document
318    describing a resource server that does not exist.
319
320    **Nothing in the document may come from a request** (§28.2 rule 8). Both
321    ``resource`` and ``authorization_servers`` are configuration; this SDK
322    offers no option to build either from the ``Host`` header, the
323    ``Forwarded``/``X-Forwarded-*`` family or the request URL, because a
324    document assembled from the request is a document an attacker can point
325    at an authorization server of their choosing — the whole handshake
326    redirected with one header.
327
328    Args:
329        resource: The resource identifier. Absolute, ``https`` (or ``http``
330            on a loopback host), with no query and no fragment. A trailing
331            slash is significant.
332        authorization_servers: The issuer identifiers of the authorization
333            servers guarding it — at least one, no duplicates, no query, no
334            fragment.
335        scopes_supported: The scope tokens this resource server understands.
336            Order is preserved, duplicates are refused, and an empty
337            sequence omits the member.
338        bearer_methods_supported: Defaults to ``("header",)``, and
339            ``("header",)`` is the only accepted value in this contract
340            version.
341        resource_documentation: Optional documentation page for a human. May
342            carry a query and a fragment; omitted from the document when
343            absent.
344
345    Returns:
346        The validated :class:`ProtectedResourceMetadata`.
347
348    Raises:
349        ValidationError: when any §28.2 rule is violated.
350
351    Example::
352
353        metadata = protected_resource_metadata(
354            resource="https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
355            authorization_servers=["https://axiam.example.com"],
356            scopes_supported=["mcp:read", "mcp:tools"],
357        )
358        metadata.metadata_path  # '/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp'
359        metadata.metadata_url   # 'https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp'
360    """
361    op = "protected_resource_metadata"
362
363    # Rule 1 + rule 2.
364    parsed = _require_absolute_uri(op, "resource", resource, _IDENTIFIER)
365
366    # Rule 3 + rule 4: at least one entry, each an issuer verbatim, no duplicates.
367    servers = list(authorization_servers)
368    if len(servers) == 0:
369        _refuse(
370            op,
371            "authorization_servers",
372            "must name at least one authorization server — a document that names "
373            "none answers none of the question the client asked",
374        )
375    seen_servers: set[str] = set()
376    resolved_servers: list[str] = []
377    for issuer in servers:
378        _require_absolute_uri(op, "authorization_servers", issuer, _IDENTIFIER)
379        if issuer in seen_servers:
380            _refuse(op, "authorization_servers", f"duplicate entry {issuer!r}")
381        seen_servers.add(issuer)
382        resolved_servers.append(issuer)
383
384    # Rule 5: NQCHAR tokens, order preserved, duplicates refused, empty omits.
385    seen_scopes: set[str] = set()
386    resolved_scopes: list[str] = []
387    for scope in scopes_supported:
388        if scope == "" or not _is_all(scope, _is_nqchar):
389            _refuse(
390                op,
391                "scopes_supported",
392                f"{scope!r} is not a scope token — one or more NQCHAR (no space, "
393                "no '\"', no '\\\\', no control character, no non-ASCII)",
394            )
395        if scope in seen_scopes:
396            _refuse(op, "scopes_supported", f"duplicate scope {scope!r}")
397        seen_scopes.add(scope)
398        resolved_scopes.append(scope)
399
400    # Rule 6: exactly ["header"].
401    methods = list(bearer_methods_supported)
402    if len(methods) != 1 or methods[0] != "header":
403        _refuse(
404            op,
405            "bearer_methods_supported",
406            f"must be exactly ['header'] in this contract version — §10's guard "
407            f"reads a bearer credential from the Authorization header alone, so "
408            f"{methods!r} would describe behaviour this SDK does not have",
409        )
410
411    # Rule 7: absolute URL, query and fragment permitted, omitted when absent.
412    if resource_documentation is not None:
413        _require_absolute_uri(op, "resource_documentation", resource_documentation, _LOCATOR)
414
415    document = ProtectedResourceMetadataDocument(
416        resource=resource,
417        authorization_servers=tuple(resolved_servers),
418        scopes_supported=tuple(resolved_scopes) if resolved_scopes else None,
419        bearer_methods_supported=("header",),
420        resource_documentation=resource_documentation,
421    )
422
423    metadata_path = _derive_metadata_path(parsed.path)
424    return ProtectedResourceMetadata(
425        document=document,
426        metadata_path=metadata_path,
427        metadata_url=f"{parsed.scheme}://{parsed.authority}{metadata_path}",
428    )

protected_resource_metadata(...) (CONTRACT.md §28.1) — build and validate the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata document this server publishes about itself, and derive the path and URL it is served at.

Validation happens here and it refuses; it never repairs. Every §28.2 rule is checked before any route exists and before any request is served, and a violation raises ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError's ~axiam_sdk.management.ValidationError sub-type. Nothing is normalised, trimmed, lowercased or re-encoded to make it pass: a value that needs adjusting is a configuration mistake an operator fixes in one line, and a helper that quietly fixed it would publish a document describing a resource server that does not exist.

Nothing in the document may come from a request (§28.2 rule 8). Both resource and authorization_servers are configuration; this SDK offers no option to build either from the Host header, the Forwarded/X-Forwarded-* family or the request URL, because a document assembled from the request is a document an attacker can point at an authorization server of their choosing — the whole handshake redirected with one header.

Args: resource: The resource identifier. Absolute, https (or http on a loopback host), with no query and no fragment. A trailing slash is significant. authorization_servers: The issuer identifiers of the authorization servers guarding it — at least one, no duplicates, no query, no fragment. scopes_supported: The scope tokens this resource server understands. Order is preserved, duplicates are refused, and an empty sequence omits the member. bearer_methods_supported: Defaults to ("header",), and ("header",) is the only accepted value in this contract version. resource_documentation: Optional documentation page for a human. May carry a query and a fragment; omitted from the document when absent.

Returns: The validated ProtectedResourceMetadata.

Raises: ValidationError: when any §28.2 rule is violated.

Example::

metadata = protected_resource_metadata(
    resource="https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
    authorization_servers=["https://axiam.example.com"],
    scopes_supported=["mcp:read", "mcp:tools"],
)
metadata.metadata_path  # '/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp'
metadata.metadata_url   # 'https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp'
